class_definitions.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
class_definitions.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
class_definitions.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
class_definitions.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
class_definitions.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

reader: one reader, reading name, description, documentation and unit together; no pipeline judge, review check or decide_batch produced any label

ruling.text: a bare species name counts ions summed over all charge states, with neutral atoms excluded
ruling.effect: a name that states a species and a definition that states the ion population only name the same quantity, so the pop-ion-only wording is agreement rather than a missing qualifier

projection.method: per-file stratified: each file's class share applied to that file's published count, summed over the 28 files

projection_under_ruling.method: the same per-file stratified projection, taken over the class the ruling gives each row

unit_check.method: for each sampled name the unit's dimension was compared against the quantity the name states

positive_control.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall
positive_control.why: a rate (s^-1) on a name that states a flux (m^-2.s^-1); the same name is listed under 'particle_flux s^-1' by the unit census already committed in this directory, which shows the dimension check finds a conflict known to be present

second_reader.reader: a separate reader, with no sight of this record's labels, and told the species-population ruling before it read
second_reader.joined_by: name, through the sheet's item id
second_reader.subset_prepared: 60 names drawn with seed 7714 across all 28 files

rows.name: current_of_antenna_strap
rows.description: Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a plasma.
rows.documentation: Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a plasma. It is a scalar line-current quantity associated with the strap itself. The strap current is the current-density flux through an oriented cross-section of the same strap: $$ I_s(t) = \int_{S_s} \mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot d\mathbf{S} $$ where $I_s(t)$ is the current of antenna strap at time $t$, $S_s$ is an oriented cross-section of that strap, $\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t)$ is the electric current density in the strap at position $\mathbf{x}$ and time $t$, and $d\mathbf{S}$ is the vector area element whose orientation sets the positive strap direction. This quantity is scoped to an antenna strap, not to an arbitrary antenna conductor, feed line, matching network, or complete antenna system. It denotes current carried by the strap material and is not a voltage, impedance, launched power, absorbed power, or a sum over multiple distinct straps. [Wave current of antenna strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) is the radio-frequency-wave specialization of this strap current and characterizes the same strap-carried current with a specified wave-current representation, such as peak amplitude or root mean square. The parent quantity identifies the common antenna-strap current shared by such specialized names without replacing their representation qualifiers. Sign convention: Positive when conventional current has a net projection along the assigned positive direction of the antenna strap.

rows.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
rows.description: Volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by fast ions of a specified species and charge state or bundle, locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: Fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to nonthermal fast ions of a specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle per unit physical volume. It encompasses local absorption and its flux-surface average, which represents deposition averaged over a magnetic flux surface. The local absorption density and its flux-surface-averaged form are defined by $$ p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}} = \sum_{z\in C}\frac{dP_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}}{dV}, \qquad p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local fast-ion absorption density, $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is its flux-surface average, $C$ is the selected set of ionic charge states, $z$ identifies an included charge state, $P_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the wave power absorbed by fast ions in that state, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average. A single-state quantity includes only that charge state; a bundle is summed over its included states, not over every charge state of the species. The recipient population excludes thermal ions. The quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent collisional redistribution, stored fast-ion energy, or volume-integrated absorbed power. This is the fast-population, direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), rather than its full net energy-source term. Summing nonoverlapping contributions over all ionic charge states gives [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density) for the same species, wave content, and spatial averaging. The [toroidal-mode-resolved counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) additionally separates this absorption by toroidal Fourier mode.

rows.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
rows.description: Signed coordinate of a neutral beam injector source-outline vertex along the injector’s first local tangential direction.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the signed first local tangential coordinate of a point on a neutral beam injector source outline. It belongs to the injector’s object-local frame and is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) to describe the outline in its tangent plane. The coordinate is defined by $$ x_1 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1 $$ where $x_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position of the source-outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the injector-local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is its positive first local tangential unit vector. The origin and orientation are determined by the neutral beam injector’s local geometric convention; this quantity is not a coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and does not specify that convention by itself. Sign convention: Positive when the outline vertex lies in the direction of the positive first local tangential basis vector from the local-frame origin.

rows.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
rows.description: Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the incident radio-frequency power arriving at its back from the source through the feed line.
rows.documentation: Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna denotes the incident radio-frequency traveling-wave power arriving at the back of the antenna through its feed line. It is the source-to-antenna component at the antenna reference plane, before reflected power is subtracted. For a single antenna, the power components referred to the same reference plane satisfy $$ P_{\mathrm{fwd}} = P_{\mathrm{launched}} + P_{\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the forward incident power, $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the net [launched power](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the [reflected power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) returning toward the source. This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna, not a sum over an antenna set. It includes only the forward-traveling component, excluding the backward-traveling reflected component. Subtracting reflected power gives net launched power; forward power is neither this net quantity nor the power subsequently absorbed by the plasma.

rows.name: forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
rows.description: Relative phase of the forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, referenced to the first module for inter-module toroidal phasing.
rows.documentation: The forward-wave phase is the relative phase angle of the complex radio-frequency power-wave phasor associated with one ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module. It describes inter-module phasing rather than an absolute phase. For selected module $i$, the relative forward-wave phase is defined by $$ \theta_i^{+} = \arg\left(\tilde{a}_i^{+}\right) - \arg\left(\tilde{a}_1^{+}\right) $$ where $\theta_i^{+}$ is the relative forward-wave phase, $i$ identifies the selected antenna module, module $1$ is the first reference module, $\tilde{a}_i^{+}$ is the complex phasor of the forward radio-frequency power wave associated with module $i$, and $\arg$ returns a phasor's phase angle. The quantity applies only to the forward wave at an antenna module and is defined relative to the first module; no absolute phase relative to a generator or external reference is implied. It concerns the electromagnetic power-wave phasor, not a plasma-particle quantity or a spatially distributed plasma field. This is the forward-wave specialization of the relative antenna phasor phase defined by [wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna). It is distinct from the relative phase of the reflected wave, [reflected phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and from the phase of the RF current carried by an antenna strap, [wave phase of an antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap). Sign convention: Positive when the selected module's forward-wave phasor leads the first reference module in phase.

rows.name: net_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
rows.description: Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the radio-frequency energy absorbed per unit time by the plasma from a specific launcher, excluding losses outside the plasma.
rows.documentation: Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which radio-frequency waves from a specific launcher transfer energy to the plasma. It includes absorption by all plasma particle populations, not only ions. The absorbed power is defined by $$ P = \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} p_{\mathrm{abs}}\,dV $$ where $P$ is the net absorbed power attributable to the launcher, $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the entire plasma volume, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the local radio-frequency energy-transfer rate per volume summed over all absorbing plasma populations and averaged over a radio-frequency cycle, and $dV$ is a volume element. This quantity applies to one launcher, not a sum over launchers. Unabsorbed wave power and dissipation outside the plasma are excluded. The [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the forward-minus-reflected power directed into the vessel before plasma absorption; it need not equal the absorbed power defined here. The [total power due to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating) sums launched power over all heating antennas and therefore differs in both absorption scope and launcher aggregation.

rows.name: parallel_peak_launched_refractive_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
rows.description: Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna. It is the signed value at the dominant spectral peak set by the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, not an algebraic maximum over all launched components.
rows.documentation: Peak value of the parallel refractive index in the lower-hybrid wave spectrum launched by an antenna is the signed parallel refractive-index coordinate of the dominant launched spectral peak. The parallel direction is taken along the local magnetic-field direction at the launcher aperture. The defining value is the refractive index associated with the peak parallel wave number of the launched spectrum: $$ N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}} = \frac{c\,k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}}{\omega} $$ where $N_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the peak launched parallel refractive index, $c$ is the speed of light, $k_{\parallel,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the parallel wave number at the dominant peak of the launched lower-hybrid spectrum, and $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency. For this quantity, the dominant peak is the main spectral peak inferred from the measured phase difference between neighboring waveguide rows, through the row-to-row phase advance per projected row separation in the parallel phasing direction. This quantity is not the algebraic maximum of $N_\parallel$ over all launched components; if the main spectral peak lies at negative $N_\parallel$, the peak value is negative.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
rows.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by thermal ions of a specified species and charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number.
rows.documentation: Toroidal-mode-resolved thermal-ion charge-state power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to thermal ions of a specified species and charge state per unit physical volume. Each contribution corresponds to one toroidal Fourier harmonic. For a magnetic flux surface, the mode-resolved deposition is defined by $$ p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} = \left\langle Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $p_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the flux-surface-averaged modal power density, $Q_{a,z}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding local volumetric rate of wave energy transfer to thermal ions, $a$ identifies the ion species, $z$ identifies its charge state, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over that magnetic flux surface. The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal ions of the selected species and charge state; neither charge states nor toroidal modes are summed. This quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent collisional energy redistribution, a local deposition value before flux-surface averaging, or volume-integrated absorbed power. The [fast-ion counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) instead describes absorption by nonthermal ions. Summing over all included toroidal harmonics recovers the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density), not its unaveraged local value.

rows.name: poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
rows.description: Signed dimensionless poloidal component of the launched lower-hybrid wave refractive-index vector, measured along increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point.
rows.documentation: The poloidal launched-wave index is the projection of the lower-hybrid launched wave refractive-index vector onto the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point. It describes the poloidal part of the launch spectrum and is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal launched-wave index](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The index is defined by $$ N_\theta = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta}{k_0} = \frac{k_\theta}{k_0} $$ where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched wave vector, $\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$, $k_\theta$ is the corresponding wave-vector projection, and $k_0 = \omega/c$ is the free-space wavenumber for angular frequency $\omega$ and speed of light $c$. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity describes the launch condition only; it is not the local poloidal wave index after propagation or interaction with the plasma. Sign convention: Positive when the launched wave-vector projection points in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$.

rows.name: power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
rows.description: Net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma through electron cyclotron heating, with source aggregation determined by scope and excluding launched or reflected power.
rows.documentation: Electron-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which electron-cyclotron-range electromagnetic waves transfer energy to the plasma, principally through resonant electron absorption. It denotes deposited plasma heating power rather than generator, launched, transmitted, or reflected power. The absorbed power is defined by the volume integral of the local electron-cyclotron heating density: $$ P_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} Q_{\mathrm{EC}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the absorbed power, $Q_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the local power-transfer density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. Source aggregation is scope-dependent; the [total electron-cyclotron heating power](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating) sums the contributions from all electron-cyclotron wave sources. The quantity is non-negative for net absorption and is distinct from [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) when that quantity includes wave absorption without restricting the mechanism to electron cyclotron heating.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
rows.description: Major-radius coordinate locating the sphere center that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the sphere that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. It identifies the mirror's geometric reference point rather than a point on the reflecting surface. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius coordinate relates to right-handed Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ through $$ R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2} $$ where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinate values in the $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity applies to the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's spherical defining geometry and represents one geometric point. It is not a plasma quantity, a surface coordinate, a mirror steering angle, or an average or integral over the mirror. The broader [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) concept is specialized here to the sphere center of the mirror. Together with the [vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), it locates the same geometric center.

rows.name: radius_of_neutral_beam_injector
rows.description: Radius of the circular ion-source surface from which neutral beams are extracted, defining the radial extent of its extraction aperture.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the radius of the circular ion-source surface from which a neutral-beam injector extracts its beam. It defines the radial extent of the extraction aperture. For a circular boundary, the radius is the distance from the surface center to any point on its circumference: $$ r_s = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}_c \right\rVert $$ where $r_s$ is the ion-source-surface radius, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position of a point on the circular boundary, $\mathbf{x}_c$ is the position of the circle center, and the norm denotes Euclidean distance. The quantity applies to one neutral-beam injector unit and only to its circular ion-source geometry. It is not an aggregate over injector units and does not represent the radius of a beamlet-group tangency surface or another injector-associated aperture. For a rectangular ion-source aperture, the corresponding transverse dimensions are given by the [first local tangential width of the neutral-beam injector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector) and [second local tangential width of the neutral-beam injector](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector), rather than by this radius.

rows.name: straight_field_line_angle
rows.description: An angular coordinate that labels position along magnetic field lines after a straight-field-line transformation, making field-line trajectories linear on each magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: A straight-field-line angle is an angular coordinate for labeling position along magnetic field lines in a magnetic-flux coordinate description. The transformation is chosen so that field-line trajectories are straight, or have constant angular slope, on each flux surface. This quantity denotes the coordinate itself rather than a mechanical steering angle, wave phase, or physical distance along a field line. Its origin, angular orientation, and selected angular direction are defined by the associated straight-field-line coordinate convention. The [poloidal straight-field-line angle](name:poloidal_straight_field_line_angle) is the poloidal specialization of this general coordinate concept. Other specializations, when defined, differ by the angular direction or coordinate convention rather than by a different underlying physical quantity. Sign convention: Positive when position advances in the defined positive direction of the straight-field-line angular coordinate.

rows.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
rows.description: Toroidal-angle coordinate of the middle reference position of a lower-hybrid antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The toroidal coordinate $\phi$ locates the middle reference position of a lower-hybrid antenna row around the machine symmetry axis. It is the angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. This coordinate specifies the row's toroidal location and does not determine its radial or vertical location. The corresponding radial location is given by the radial coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna row. Sign convention: Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above along the $+Z$ direction.

rows.name: total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
rows.description: Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant electron-cyclotron interactions. It excludes launched, transmitted, reflected, and unabsorbed shine-through power.
rows.documentation: Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant interaction with electrons at the electron cyclotron frequency or its harmonics. It is an absorbed heating power, not the generated, launched, transmitted, reflected, or unabsorbed radiofrequency power. The total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power is the sum of the net absorbed powers from the contributing electron-cyclotron sources: $$ P_\mathrm{EC} = \sum_{s=1}^{N_\mathrm{EC}} P_{\mathrm{EC},s} $$ where $N_\mathrm{EC}$ is the number of contributing electron-cyclotron sources, $P_{\mathrm{EC},s}$ is the net electron-cyclotron power absorbed by the plasma from source $s$ expressed in watts, and $P_\mathrm{EC}$ is the total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power expressed in watts. The per-source contribution is [power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating](name:power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating). This quantity is non-negative and is zero when no electron-cyclotron power is absorbed by the plasma; it is a component of [total_external_heating_power](name:total_external_heating_power) when total external heating is formed over all auxiliary heating methods.

rows.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
rows.description: Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
rows.documentation: Vertical $Z$-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row is the projection of that row reference point onto $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For a row reference point with position vector $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}}$, the coordinate is defined by: $$ Z_{\mathrm{row}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}} \cdot \hat{Z} $$ where $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This is a row-level coordinate and is distinct from the antenna-level [vertical coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It is distinct from the row vertical extent. Sign convention: Positive when the row reference point lies in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame from the $Z=0$ plane.

rows.name: vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group
rows.description: Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the distance along the neutral-beam line from the group’s ion source to the point where the group’s vertical extent is minimized.
rows.documentation: Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the path length along the neutral-beam line from the beamlet group's ion source to the group vertical focus. The group vertical focus is the location at which the collective beamlet envelope has its minimum vertical extent, with vertical measured parallel to $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Using an along-beam coordinate $s$ that increases from the ion source along the neutral-beam line, the focal length is defined by $$ f_v = s_f - s_0, \qquad w_v(s_f) = \min_s w_v(s) $$ where $f_v$ is the vertical focal length of the beamlet group, $s_0$ is the ion-source position on the along-beam coordinate, $s_f$ is the vertical-focus position, and $w_v(s)$ is the collective vertical envelope extent of the beamlet group at position $s$. The quantity applies to one beamlet group and aggregates all beamlets in that group through their collective vertical envelope. It is not a per-beamlet focal length and not a whole-unit focal length formed by combining multiple groups; the distance is along the beam-line path rather than a vertical separation. It is distinct from the source-surface vertical width of a beamlet group and from any vertical extent at locations other than the focus; those are transverse extents, whereas this quantity is the along-beam separation to the location of the minimum. It is the vertical counterpart of the horizontal focal length of a beamlet group, which uses the minimum horizontal extent instead of the minimum vertical extent.

rows.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
rows.description: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna specifies the relative angular offset of coherent radio-frequency excitations at selected straps or modules.
rows.documentation: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the relative phase of a coherent radio-frequency excitation associated with a selected strap or module. It describes excitation phasing rather than an absolute phase independent of a reference. For selected and reference excitations, the relative phase is defined by $$ \varphi = \arg\!\left(A_{\mathrm{sel}} A_{\mathrm{ref}}^*\right) \pmod{2\pi} $$ where $\varphi$ is the wave phase, $A_{\mathrm{sel}}$ is the selected complex excitation phasor, $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the coherent reference excitation phasor, the superscript $*$ denotes complex conjugation, and $\arg$ extracts the complex argument. Both phasors must be nonzero and refer to the same radio-frequency component. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$. The scope includes relative phasing between antenna straps or modules, without summation or averaging over elements. The excitation quantity, reference excitation, reference planes, and temporal phasor convention must be specified. Feed-voltage phase and traveling power-wave phase are distinct realizations and are not interchangeable without their electrical relationship. Relative element phasing affects interference between excitations and therefore the launched wave spectrum and current-drive efficiency. The [forward-wave phase](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) specializes this quantity to forward power-wave phasors referenced to the first module; that reference is not imposed on the general quantity. The [wave phase of an antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap) specifically identifies the phase of its radio-frequency current phasor. Neither phase quantity includes excitation magnitude. Sign convention: Positive when the selected excitation phasor leads the reference excitation phasor in phase under the declared temporal phasor convention.

rows.name: electron_temperature_at_pellet_path
rows.description: Background-plasma electron temperature evaluated locally along the pellet’s ablation trajectory, describing the thermal state encountered by the pellet during transit.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the local energy-equivalent temperature of background plasma electrons at positions along the pellet trajectory. It describes the plasma encountered by the pellet, not the thermal state of pellet material or an average over the entire trajectory. For an isotropic electron population, the energy-equivalent temperature is defined by $$ T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e\rangle $$ where $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as an energy, and $\langle E_e\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron. The quantity applies only to background electrons and is evaluated locally along the pellet path; it is not charge-state aggregated, path-averaged, or a pellet ablation rate. The corresponding [electron density at the pellet path](name:electron_density_at_pellet_path) describes the local free-electron population at the same trajectory locations, while this quantity specifies its thermal energy state.

rows.name: helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top
rows.description: Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all helium-3 ion charge states.
rows.documentation: Helium-3 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local volumetric abundance of helium-3 ions, including all ionization states. It applies to the helium-3 ion population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \sum_z n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}} $$ where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local helium-3 ion number density, $n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of helium-3 ions in charge state $z$, and $z$ is the positive integer ion charge state. This quantity is evaluated locally at the pedestal top defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The sum includes all helium-3 ion charge states and excludes neutral helium-3; the quantity is neither a flux-surface average nor a volume average. It is the helium-3 species component of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), whereas [helium-3 density at the limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter) refers to a different spatial locus.

rows.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
rows.description: Line-of-sight average of the number density of positively charged tungsten ions, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the line-of-sight average of the charge-state-summed number density of positively charged tungsten ions. $$ \bar n_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{L}} \left[\sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)\right] \, dl $$ Here, $\bar n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten-ion number density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the specified averaging line, $L$ is its total length, $l$ is distance along that line, $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $Z$. The sum includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten. The quantity applies to the aggregate tungsten-ion population along the specified line and is averaged over that line rather than evaluated locally or averaged over volume. It therefore differs from the local or otherwise spatially averaged [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) by its line-of-sight aggregation, and from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density) by using a line rather than the enclosed plasma volume.

rows.name: current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive
rows.description: Vector electric-current-density contribution generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients.
rows.documentation: Current density due to bootstrap current drive is the vector contribution to electric current density generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients. It represents conventional electric-current flow produced by this drive mechanism, before selecting any particular component or projection. The quantity is scoped to the bootstrap-driven contribution only. It excludes current-density contributions from externally driven current, inductive electric fields, neutral beams, radio-frequency waves, or any total current density that aggregates multiple drive mechanisms. This parent quantity denotes the full vector bootstrap-current-density contribution. Component or projection quantities are more specific descendants; for example, [parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive) is the field-aligned projection of this vector along the magnetic-field direction, not a synonym for the full vector. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component represents conventional current flowing in the positive direction of that component or projection.

rows.name: current_due_to_fusion_reactions
rows.description: Net parallel plasma current generated by fusion reactions, associated with fast alpha particles produced by deuterium–tritium reactions and distinct from other non-inductive current-drive mechanisms.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the net plasma current attributable to fusion reactions within the plasma, associated with fast alpha particles produced by deuterium–tritium reactions. It represents the parallel current contribution rather than the total plasma current. The defining relation is $$ I_{\mathrm{fus}} = \int_S \mathbf{j}_{\alpha} \cdot \mathbf{b}\, dS $$ where $I_{\mathrm{fus}}$ is the fusion-reaction-driven current, $\mathbf{j}_{\alpha}$ is the current-density vector carried by the fusion-born fast-alpha population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field direction, and $S$ is the cross-sectional surface through which the parallel current is evaluated; $dS$ is an element of that surface. The quantity is a net signed aggregation over the fusion-born alpha population and the relevant plasma cross section. It includes only the current attributable to fusion reactions and is not a local current density, a current magnitude, or an all-population current. It excludes current contributions driven by other mechanisms and must not be interpreted as the total plasma current or the total non-inductive current. It is an additive contribution to the non-inductive current balance. Sign convention: Positive when the fusion-reaction-driven conventional current is parallel to the local magnetic-field direction.

rows.name: current_of_divertor
rows.description: Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
rows.documentation: The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current. The current is defined by $$ I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA $$ where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the plasma toward the material. This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and [current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies to an individual tile. Sign convention: Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows from the plasma into the divertor material.

rows.name: electron_power_at_outer_divertor_target
rows.description: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons, integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface.
rows.documentation: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface is the target-integrated electron energy-transfer rate to the material surface of that target. The outer divertor target is the target on the larger-major-radius side in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The deposited electron power is the surface integral of the local electron energy-flux density directed into the wetted outer-target area: $$ P_{e,\mathrm{outer}} = \int_{A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}} q_{e,\perp}\,dA $$ where $P_{e,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the electron power at the outer divertor target, $A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, and $q_{e,\perp}$ is the electron energy-flux density directed from the plasma into the target material. This is the electron-channel component of power at the outer divertor target; ion, neutral, radiation, and other non-electron contributions are excluded. It is the outer-target counterpart of [electron power at the inner divertor target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

rows.name: ion_fluence_at_divertor_target
rows.description: Cumulative incident ion-particle dose delivered to a divertor target, with each ion counted once across all species and charge states.
rows.documentation: Ion fluence at a divertor target is the cumulative number of incident ions per unit target area over a specified time interval. It is the ion-only component of fluence at the divertor target, including all ionic species and charge states while counting each incident ion once. $$ \Phi_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \left[\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}} \Gamma_{\perp,s}(t)\right] \, dt $$ Here, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the ion fluence, $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the interval endpoints in seconds, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion species and charge states, and $\Gamma_{\perp,s}$ is the incident normal particle-flux density for state $s$, in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. The flux is directed from the plasma toward the target surface. Neutral atoms, molecules, and nonparticle channels are excluded.

rows.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
rows.description: Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for oxygen ions at the sheath entrance, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
rows.documentation: Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the oxygen-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). The local oxygen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle count: $$ n_{\rm O} = \frac{dN_{\rm O}}{dV} $$ where $N_{\rm O}$ is the total number of oxygen ions in a small plasma volume $V$ centered at the sheath entrance on the plasma side of the divertor target. This quantity applies to the oxygen-ion population at the specified divertor target and sums the number densities of all positive oxygen ionization states, counting each ion once. Neutral oxygen atoms are excluded; therefore, it is distinct from [oxygen_density](name:oxygen_density), which includes neutral oxygen as well as charged oxygen states. The target-specific quantity has the same charge-state-summed convention as [neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target), while [oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary) represents the corresponding oxygen-ion density at the plasma boundary without this divertor-target locus.

rows.name: plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
rows.description: Plasma-ion power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the neutral-particle recombination channel.
rows.documentation: This quantity captures the plasma-ion recombination power delivered to a single divertor target, representing energy deposited when plasma ions recombine at or near the plasma-material interface. It excludes the neutral-particle recombination channel quantified by [neutral-particle recombination power](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination). The plasma-ion contribution is obtained from the total target recombination power by subtracting the neutral-particle contribution: $$ P_{\rm plasma,target} = P_{\rm rec,target} - P_{\rm neutral,target} $$ where $P_{\rm plasma,target}$ is this plasma-ion recombination power, $P_{\rm rec,target}$ is the [total recombination power at the divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), and $P_{\rm neutral,target}$ is the neutral-particle contribution. This is the single-target plasma-ion component of recombination power, distinct from [total divertor recombination power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which aggregates over all divertor target surfaces and includes both plasma-ion and neutral-particle channels.

rows.name: power_due_to_recombination
rows.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing materials by recombination processes, encompassing both plasma-ion recombination and surface recombination of neutral atoms, without restriction to a particular surface location.
rows.documentation: Recombination power is the heat load delivered to plasma-facing materials when ions recover electrons and transition to neutral states, releasing ionization potential energy and residual kinetic energy at or near material surfaces. Two principal channels contribute: sheath-accelerated plasma-ion recombination at target surfaces, and surface recombination of neutral atoms into molecules, which deposits the molecular binding energy directly into the wall or divertor plate material. The integrated power from recombination events over a wetted area $A$ is: $$P_\text{rec} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s \, E_s \, dA$$ where $\Gamma_s$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ is the incident particle flux density for species $s$ and $E_s$ [J] is the energy released per recombination event for that species, including ionization potential and kinetic contributions. This power channel is intrinsically non-negative and becomes particularly significant in detached and partially detached divertor regimes, where volumetric ion-electron recombination upstream of the strike point redistributes energy deposition away from the target. Location-specific realizations include [power deposited on a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), the [total over the full divertor assembly](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), and power at first-wall surfaces. The neutral recombination particle flux produced in these processes is characterized by [neutral_energy_flux_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

rows.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_convection
rows.description: Power deposited on all divertor targets by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
rows.documentation: Convective power at all divertor targets quantifies the energy transported to those targets by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off layer. It comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions carried by convective plasma particle flux into the material surfaces, summed over all divertor targets. The all-target convective divertor power is the sum of the incident convective energy flux over the wetted surfaces of the divertor targets: $$ P_{\mathrm{conv,div}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{A_k} \sum_s \Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}} \left(h_{s,k} + \frac{1}{2} m_s |\mathbf{u}_{s,k}|^2\right) \, dA $$ where $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of divertor target surfaces, $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $s$ labels incident species in the convective channel, including streaming ion and electron species. $\Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the particle-flux density into the material, defined by the positive-into-target surface-normal projection $n_{s,k}\max(\mathbf{u}_{s,k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k},0)$; $n_{s,k}$ is the particle density, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k}$ is the surface normal directed from the plasma into the target, $h_{s,k}$ is the thermal enthalpy per particle, $m_s$ is the particle mass, and $\mathbf{u}_{s,k}$ is the directed flow velocity of the incident particles. This quantity is the all-divertor-target realization of [convective power](name:power_due_to_convection); the corresponding single-target quantity is [convective power at a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), and the broader plasma-facing-surface counterpart is [convective power at plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). It excludes [conductive divertor power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction), radiative deposition, and [recombination-related divertor plasma power](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which are separate channels of the divertor power balance.

rows.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
rows.description: Total power deposited on all divertor target surfaces by recombination processes, comprising both the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels summed over the full divertor assembly.
rows.documentation: Total divertor recombination power is the combined rate at which recombination processes at or near the target surfaces of the divertor assembly release energy into the material, integrated over all targets. It is the divertor-surface counterpart of the volumetric [power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination) and unifies two physically distinct deposition channels: $$ P_\mathrm{rec,div} = P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} + P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral} $$ where $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is [plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy deposited when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the material surface, and $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is [neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy carried by neutral particles undergoing recombination reactions at the plasma-material interface. This quantity is computed in edge-plasma codes that track ion and neutral fluxes to the targets and apply sheath-energy coefficients along with recombination cross-sections to determine surface deposition. It represents one component of the total divertor heat load alongside conducted, convected, and radiative contributions, and becomes a more prominent fraction of that load in detached or partially detached divertor regimes where volumetric recombination upstream suppresses the ion current reaching the targets.

rows.name: tungsten_density_at_divertor_target
rows.description: Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
rows.documentation: Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tungsten-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). The charge-state-summed tungsten number density is defined by $$ n_W = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{W^{Z+}} $$ where $n_W$ is the total local number density of tungsten ions, $n_{W^{Z+}}$ is the local number density of tungsten ions with positive charge state $Z$, and $Z$ is the integer tungsten ionization state from 1 through 74. This quantity applies only to tungsten ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It includes every positive tungsten ionization state once, without charge-state weighting, and excludes neutral tungsten atoms and ions of all other elements. The charge-state sum makes this the species-level tungsten component of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). Its divertor-target locus distinguishes it from [tungsten_density_at_limiter](name:tungsten_density_at_limiter), which describes tungsten ion density at a limiter, and from tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies at the plasma boundary.

rows.name: vertical_length_of_divertor_target
rows.description: Non-negative vertical span of a divertor target surface, defined by the difference between its maximum and minimum Z coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The vertical extent of a divertor target is the range of vertical positions occupied by its surface, rather than the vertical position of its center. $$ H_Z = Z_{\\max} - Z_{\\min} $$ where $H_Z$ is the vertical span, and $Z_{\\max}$ and $Z_{\\min}$ are respectively the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates over the target surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This extent complements the [radial length of the divertor target](name:radial_length_of_divertor_target) and is distinct from the [Z coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), which locates its surface center.

rows.name: boron_density
rows.description: Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+.
rows.documentation: Boron density is the elemental boron particle density, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included in one additive quantity. $$ n_B = \sum_{Z=0}^{5} n_{B,Z} $$ where $n_B$ is the elemental boron density, $Z$ is the boron ionic charge state with $Z=0$ denoting neutral boron, and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density of boron in state $Z$. The quantity is the underlying boron density field; [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density) and [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density) are distinct averages of it. It excludes no boron charge state but is not a charge-state-specific or charge-weighted density.

rows.name: density_at_pedestal_maximum
rows.description: Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal locus of maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. It is a density value at that locus, not a density gradient.
rows.documentation: Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density evaluated at the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the steep mid-pedestal locus of maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. The word maximum identifies the peak-gradient pedestal locus, not a maximum of the density value itself. The defining relation is the evaluation of the selected density function at that flux-coordinate locus: $$ n_{\mathrm{ped,max}} = n(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}) $$ where $n_{\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the density at pedestal maximum, $n(\psi_N)$ is the selected plasma-particle number density as a function of the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\psi_N$, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$ is the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). This parent quantity is species- or population-generic; concrete children, such as [electron density at pedestal maximum](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum), specialize the selected particle population without changing the locus definition. When the selected population is a species with charge states, the species-level density is summed over all charge states unless a charge-state-resolved name explicitly identifies one charge state. It excludes pedestal-top density and any local slope or maximum-gradient magnitude with respect to $\psi_N$; those quantities are distinct from the density value evaluated at this locus.

rows.name: density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Particle number density of a selected plasma population evaluated at the plasma boundary, the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
rows.documentation: Particle number density at the plasma boundary is the amount of a selected particle population per physical volume at the boundary of magnetically confined plasma. The population is intentionally unspecified by this parent quantity and is fixed by each specialized instance. The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_P(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_P(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_P$ is the number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_P$ is the velocity distribution function of population $P$, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The selected population may be an electron population, an ion or impurity population, a neutral population, an elemental population, or an effective isotope mixture. The aggregation convention is additive over exactly the particles included in population $P$; inclusion of neutral particles and summation over charge states are specialization-dependent and are not fixed by this subject-less parent quantity. This boundary quantity is distinct from [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) and [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter), which use different loci. Specialized instances fix the population and its aggregation convention: [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) selects electrons, while [krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary) selects krypton ions with charge-state aggregation. Elemental variants such as [boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary) may include both neutral atoms and ionic charge states. When population and aggregation are held fixed, the corresponding boundary value is the locus-specific counterpart of density evaluated at another defined plasma location.

rows.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for that effective species evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region. The local effective deuterium-tritium number density is the zeroth velocity moment of its distribution function at a boundary point: $$ n_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v $$ where $n_{DT}$ is the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-pseudo-species number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity of the effective pseudo-species, $f_{DT}$ is its phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies to the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture represented as one effective pseudo-species, rather than to separate deuterium and tritium populations. It is a local boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume, and no additional charge-state aggregation is implied by the effective-species representation. It is the deuterium-tritium-specific instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). Unlike flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary, it denotes the local value at the plasma boundary rather than an average over that last closed magnetic flux surface.

rows.name: edge_localized_mode_frequency
rows.description: Rate of recurrent edge-localized mode events during an ELMing H-mode phase, expressing the cadence of pedestal-relaxation bursts rather than their amplitude or exhaust.
rows.documentation: The edge-localized mode frequency is the event rate of recurrent pedestal-relaxation bursts during an ELMing H-mode phase. It characterizes the cadence of ELM events, not their amplitude, duration, expelled particle content, or transient energy. $$ f_{\mathrm{ELM}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{ELM}}}{\Delta t} $$ where $f_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the ELM event frequency, $N_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the number of identified ELM events, and $\Delta t$ is the elapsed interval over which those events are counted. The interval must represent the ELMing phase being characterized; isolated events outside that phase are excluded.

rows.name: electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
rows.description: Radial e-folding decay length of the electron heat flux in the scrape-off layer, defined by the inverse magnitude of its outward logarithmic gradient.
rows.documentation: The electron heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial distance over which the electron heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its separatrix value. It characterizes the spatial scale of electron heat exhaust across the open-field-line region and specializes the channel-unspecified [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). The decay length is defined as the inverse magnitude of the outward logarithmic gradient of the electron heat flux: $$ \lambda_{q,e} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_e}{\partial r} \right|^{-1} $$ where $q_e$ is the electron heat flux and $r$ is radial distance measured outward from the separatrix into the SOL. This quantity includes only the electron heat channel and is distinct from the corresponding [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). As the magnitude of a logarithmic gradient, the decay length is non-negative.

rows.name: flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of ions of a specified species at the plasma boundary, flux-surface averaged with inverse poloidal-flux-gradient weighting, summed over all charge states, and excluding neutral atoms and molecules.
rows.documentation:
Number density of ion The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \langle n_iangle = \oint n_i\,dS/|
abla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|
abla\psi| $$ where $\langle n_iangle$ is the averaged ion number density, $n_i$ is the local [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) of the represented ion species, $i$ is the ion-species label, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) whose gradient magnitude is $|
abla\psi|$. This quantity is evaluated on the confined-plasma side of the plasma boundary. It is summed over all charge states of the represented ion species and excludes neutral atoms and molecules; distinct ion species are not implicitly combined. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value, volume average, or chord average. The average is formed from the local [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) by applying inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting over the surface. It differs from the [flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), which additionally aggregates charged-ion densities across ion species. The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

rows.name: flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of all charged ion species at the plasma boundary, summed over charge states and excluding neutral particles.
rows.documentation:
Number density of ion The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \langle n_iangle = \oint n_i\,dS/|
abla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|
abla\psi| $$ where $\langle n_iangle$ is the averaged total ion number density, $n_i$ is the local total ion number density, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|
abla\psi|$. This quantity includes all charged ion species and is summed over their positive charge states; neutral particles are excluded. It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point value, a volume average, or a neutral-inclusive density. It is the averaged counterpart of the local [total ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), replacing that pointwise value with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting. It differs from the [line-averaged total ion density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), which averages the same charge-state-summed ion population along a specified plasma chord rather than over the plasma-boundary flux surface. The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface. Related quantities: [flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), [flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

rows.name: flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of xenon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral xenon.
rows.documentation:
Number density of xenon The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}angle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\,dS/|
abla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|
abla\psi| $$ where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}angle$ is the averaged xenon-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the local xenon-ion number density, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|
abla\psi|$. This quantity is charge-state-summed over xenon ions and is not a local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes neutral xenon. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [xenon ion density at the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting replacing the pointwise value by its surface mean. It differs from the [volume-averaged xenon density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages over the plasma volume rather than over the plasma-boundary surface. The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface. Related quantities: [flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary), [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

rows.name: helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charge states.
rows.documentation: Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the helium-4 ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion population at that locus. The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_q\int f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the ionic charge-state index, $f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This quantity applies only to helium-4 ions, is evaluated locally at the boundary, includes all helium-4 ionic charge states, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms. As a species-specific instance of [particle number density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), it fixes the otherwise unspecified population to helium-4 ions. It differs from flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma boundary, which averages the same charge-state-summed population over the boundary surface, and from [helium-3 density at the plasma boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), which selects a different helium isotope.

rows.name: hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all hydrogen ion charge states.
rows.documentation: Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the hydrogen-ion population on the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_H(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_H(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_H$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_H$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary and is summed over the included hydrogen ion charge states. It excludes neutral hydrogen and is distinct from electron density and from the total ion population represented by ion_density_at_plasma_boundary. The corresponding surface-averaged quantity, flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary, applies the same hydrogen-ion population to an average over the boundary surface rather than a local evaluation. The subject-unspecified parent [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) defines the common boundary-density concept, while this quantity fixes the population as hydrogen ions.

rows.name: iron_density
rows.description: Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
rows.documentation: Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma, aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention. The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as: $$ n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state $z$. Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance calculations. This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density averages the local density over a magnetic flux surface, [line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a chord-integrated value divided by path length, and [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key radial locations such as [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis), iron_density_at_pedestal, and [iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).

rows.name: lithium_density_at_pedestal_top
rows.description: Local number density of charged lithium ions at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all lithium ionization states and excluding neutral lithium.
rows.documentation: Lithium-ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local concentration of charged lithium particles at the pedestal's inner shoulder, where the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) identifies the evaluation location. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the total charged-lithium number density, $q$ is the lithium ionization charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of lithium ions in charge state $q$. The aggregation includes Li$^+$, Li$^{2+}$, and Li$^{3+}$ and excludes neutral lithium. This quantity is a local value at the pedestal top, not a line average such as [line-averaged lithium density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density) or a flux-surface average such as [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary). Its species scope is lithium only, and its charge-state aggregation is a sum over all charged lithium ionization states.

rows.name: lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.description: Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
rows.documentation: Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the lithium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{3}\int f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the lithium ionization-state index, $f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for lithium ions in charge state $Z+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is local at the plasma boundary and is not averaged over the boundary flux surface. It includes lithium ions from Li+ through Li3+, summed over these charge states, and excludes neutral lithium. It is the lithium-specific specialization of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The corresponding flux-surface-averaged quantity, flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary, applies a flux-surface average to the same charge-state-summed lithium-ion density. The boundary locus also distinguishes this quantity from [lithium density at the limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which is evaluated at a limiter rather than at the plasma boundary.

rows.name: momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
rows.description: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged.
rows.documentation: In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures can produce momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions such as the scrape-off layer and divertor. A flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_m$ is introduced to bound the effective flux: the limited momentum-flux density magnitude cannot exceed $\alpha_m$ times a free-streaming reference scale, while the sign follows the underlying diffusive flux direction. The limited momentum-flux density $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is formed by the harmonic-mean combination: $$ \Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}} $$ where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} = m n v_{\mathrm{th}}^2$ is the free-streaming scale with $m$ the particle mass, $n$ the number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th}}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$; when $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \ll \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the diffusive value is recovered unchanged. Specializations target individual projection directions, such as parallel_momentum_coefficient for field-aligned transport, and individual particle populations, such as ion_state_momentum_coefficient for specific ion charge states or parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient for neutral-particle parallel transport. The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative; values in the range 0.1–1 are common in edge-plasma simulations, selected by calibration against experimental separatrix and divertor data.

rows.name: neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
rows.description: Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
rows.documentation: Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The quantity denotes the diamagnetic contribution without selecting a particular flux direction or transported momentum component. The contribution is defined componentwise by: $$ \Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \rho_{\mathrm{ns}} v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} u_{b,\mathrm{ns}} $$ where $\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum flux, $a$ is its flux-direction index, $b$ is its transported-momentum index, $\rho_{\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state mass density, $v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, and $u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state linear flow velocity. This is the neutral-state specialization of [momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes contributions attributed to other transport mechanisms and is closely related to [neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux). Sign convention: Positive when the transported neutral-state momentum crosses the oriented reference surface along its positive flux direction.

rows.name: nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
rows.description: Local number density of nitrogen ions at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
rows.documentation: Nitrogen ion number density at the H-mode pedestal top is the local number of nitrogen ions per physical volume, with all ionic charge states aggregated. The charge-state sum is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the total nitrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the number density of nitrogen ions in charge state $q$, and $q$ is the positive integer ionic charge state from singly ionized through fully stripped nitrogen. This quantity applies locally at the inner shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).
