The accumulated release at path distance $\ell$ is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{abl}}(\ell)=\int_{\ell_0}^{\ell}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{abl}}}{d\ell'}\,d\ell' $$ where $N_{\mathrm{abl}}$ is the dimensionless released-particle count, $\ell$ and $\ell'$ are distances along the pellet trajectory in m, $\ell_0$ is the trajectory entry position, and $dN_{\mathrm{abl}}/d\ell'$ is the local ablation release per unit path distance. The count is nondecreasing along the trajectory when the ablation release rate is nonnegative. It represents deposited pellet material and is distinct from the initial pellet inventory given by count of pellet.

rows.name: accumulated_silane_count_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of silane molecules delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 equivalent electrons per neutral SiH4 molecule.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral silane (SiH4) molecules delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented on an equivalent-electron basis. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 18N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}} $$ where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}$ is the cumulative number of neutral silane molecules delivered after breakdown. The factor 18 is the sum of silicon's 14 atomic-number electrons and four hydrogen atoms' one atomic-number electron each. The scope is silane delivered after plasma breakdown specifically by gas injection. The count is cumulative over all such delivery and is not an instantaneous rate, a count of free electrons in the plasma, or a charge-state-resolved inventory; subsequent ionization, transport, retention, and removal do not change the delivered-inventory convention. The corresponding instantaneous quantity is the [silane source rate](name:silane_source_rate). Like the [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), this quantity uses an equivalent-electron aggregation, but silane contributes 18 equivalent electrons per molecule rather than one per hydrogen atom.

rows.name: accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Cumulative number of tritium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each tritium atom corresponds to one equivalent electron.
rows.documentation: The accumulated tritium count due to gas injection is the running total of tritium ($^3\mathrm{H}$) atoms introduced to the plasma vessel through gas injection valves, accumulated continuously from plasma breakdown onward. The quantity is dimensionless, representing each injected atom as an equivalent-electron contribution scaled by its atomic number. For tritium, whose atomic number is $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron inventory equals the raw atom count directly: $$ N_\mathrm{eq} = Z \cdot N_\mathrm{atoms} = N_\mathrm{atoms} $$ where $N_\mathrm{atoms}$ is the total number of tritium atoms injected after breakdown. The equivalent-electron convention provides a species-independent basis for comparing injected particle inventories — for higher-$Z$ species such as argon ($Z = 18$), the multiplier is correspondingly larger. This is the time-integrated form of tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection, accumulating monotonically as gas is puffed after breakdown. Tritium introduced before breakdown is tracked separately as tritium_prefill_count. The deuterium analog in the same equivalent-electron framework is [deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection).

rows.name: accumulated_xenon_count_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Cumulative post-breakdown xenon inventory delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 54 count units assigned to each xenon atom.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative inventory of xenon atoms introduced by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented using an equivalent-electron counting convention. It denotes delivered xenon inventory rather than instantaneous xenon content in the plasma. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} N_{\mathrm{Xe}} = 54 N_{\mathrm{Xe}} $$ where $N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron xenon inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon atomic number, and $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the cumulative number of xenon atoms delivered by post-breakdown gas injection. The scope is limited to xenon atoms delivered after plasma breakdown, with contributions from all post-breakdown gas-injection events cumulatively summed. No other injected species are included, and the quantity is not an instantaneous injection rate. The equivalent-electron convention uses the xenon atomic number and does not represent the actual number of free plasma electrons supplied by xenon; it is independent of the xenon ionization state. Gas introduced before breakdown is excluded and belongs to the distinct [accumulated xenon prefill inventory](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count), which provides the corresponding prefill contribution.

rows.name: argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron argon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected argon atom with Z = 18 contributes 18 equivalent-electron counts.
rows.documentation: The argon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral argon with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts each injected neutral argon atom as 18 equivalent electrons because neutral argon has 18 electrons; this is an inventory-accounting convention, not a statement about subsequent ionization or confinement. The defining relation for injected argon is: $$ \dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} $$ where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the raw argon-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon. This quantity is the argon-species member of [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), and differs from raw gas-particle source rates by the factor $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$. Sign convention: Positive when argon is delivered into the plasma vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

rows.name: ethane_source_rate
rows.description: Instantaneous ethane-gas injection rate into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second, with 18 equivalent electrons assigned to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which neutral ethane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel, converted to an equivalent-electron rate. It counts the electrons associated with neutral molecular composition, not free electrons produced by ionization. $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t) $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral ethane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, and $t$ is time in seconds. The factor $18=2\times6+6\times1$ is the total atomic-number electron count of one C2H6 molecule. This is an instantaneous rate rather than a cumulative inventory; its time integral gives the accumulated equivalent-electron count represented by [accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count). It excludes other molecular species, including the distinct [ethylene source rate](name:ethylene_source_rate).

rows.name: minimum_gas_flow
rows.description: Minimum gas flow is the smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower bound of its controllable range.
rows.documentation: Minimum gas flow is the lower reliable operating limit of the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It identifies the smallest controllable value of the aggregate gas stream throughput, rather than a molecular-species flow or particle-number rate. The pressure-volume throughput represented by this quantity is defined as $$ Q_g = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt} $$ where $Q_g$ is gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is gas pressure at the flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing that boundary, and $t$ is time. This quantity applies to the aggregate gas stream delivered through an injection system across a defined flow boundary. The stream is not restricted to a particular molecular species or charge state, and this quantity is distinct from mass flow and particle-number rate. Its defining distinction is the lower reliable operating bound, rather than an unrestricted instantaneous throughput. The gas flow quantity defines the same pressure-volume throughput without imposing a lower-limit condition; minimum gas flow is its lower reliable operating bound. Conversely, [maximum gas flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) is the upper reliable operating bound, so the two quantities delimit the controllable range rather than represent different throughput definitions.

rows.name: molecular_neutral_species_flow_at_outlet
rows.description: Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is defined by the outlet partial pressure of that species and the corresponding effective pumping speed, not by total neutral pressure.
rows.documentation: Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is species-specific and uses the outlet partial pressure of that molecular neutral species rather than the [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure). The outlet throughput is defined by the product of the outlet species partial pressure and the effective pumping speed for that species: $$ Q_{s,\mathrm{out}} = p_{s,\mathrm{out}} S_{s,\mathrm{out}} $$ where $Q_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is this molecular neutral species flow at the outlet, $p_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the outlet partial pressure of molecular neutral species $s$, and $S_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the effective pumping speed for species $s$ at the outlet. This quantity is an outlet removal throughput, distinct from a gas source into the vessel such as [gas injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection). It is the molecular, species-resolved outlet form of neutral species flow and a species-specific specialization of gas flow. Sign convention: Positive when the molecular neutral species is removed through the outlet in the pumping direction away from the vessel.

rows.name: neon_prefill_count
rows.description: Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 equivalent electrons per atom.
rows.documentation: Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral neon atom contributes 10 equivalent electrons. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}(t)\,dt $$ where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the neon equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-neon atom count, both pure counts; $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the atomic number of neon; $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neutral-neon atom introduction rate in atoms s$^{-1}$; and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times, with $t$ in s. This quantity includes only neutral neon introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not a statement that the gas is fully ionized during prefill. It is the neon component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) represents distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different noble gas.

rows.name: power_of_plant_system
rows.description: Real electrical power assigned at a plant-system boundary, representing absorbed load, net generation balance, or an aggregate of included system loads.
rows.documentation: Real electrical power is the rate of electrical-energy transfer or accounting associated with a plant system at its electrical boundary. It excludes reactive power and other non-electrical energy flows. The instantaneous power is defined by $$ P = \frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t} $$ where $E$ is the electrical energy associated with the accounting boundary and $t$ is time. The accounting convention is fixed by the specialized quantity. Absorbed power of a plant system represents one-way incoming electrical load, net power of a plant system represents generation minus internal consumption and is positive for net export, and total power of a plant system is the sum of the loads of all included systems. These forms are distinct applications of the same plant-boundary electrical-power concept.

rows.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment
rows.description: Azimuthal location of a shattered-pellet fragment’s center of mass around the machine symmetry axis, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal angle $\phi_f$ of a shattered-pellet fragment’s center of mass. It specifies that position around the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, whose coordinate values are $(R,\phi,Z)$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. Using Cartesian coordinates $(x_f,y_f,z_f)$ of the same center of mass in the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, the toroidal angle is $$ \phi_f = \operatorname{atan2}(y_f,x_f) $$ where $\operatorname{atan2}$ gives the oriented azimuth relative to the defined $\phi=0$ direction. The angle is periodic modulo $2\pi$ and is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate at the shattering position](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_shattering_position) and the [toroidal coordinate of the intact pellet](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet). Sign convention: Positive when the fragment center of mass lies in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: total_heating_power_due_to_fusion_reactions
rows.description: Gross thermal power delivered to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric conversion cycle from fusion reactions, including blanket energy multiplication.
rows.documentation: Total fusion-attributed heating power is the gross thermal input delivered to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric conversion cycle. It combines heat released by fusion reactions with additional thermal power produced by nuclear energy multiplication in the blanket. $$ P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}} = P_{\mathrm{fusion}} + P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}} $$ Here, $P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the total fusion-attributed thermal power supplied to the conversion cycle, $P_{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the thermal power released by fusion reactions and entering the plant heat stream, and $P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}}$ is the additional thermal power generated by energy multiplication in the blanket. The quantity is aggregated over all included fusion-reaction and blanket-multiplication contributions at the plant conversion-cycle boundary. It is a gross thermal input, not local plasma heating or a power density. The cumulative plasma heating or energy-transfer quantity [power at an inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface) describes energy associated with a plasma region and is therefore distinct from this plant-level cycle input.

rows.name: total_neutral_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of neutral gas introduced into the vessel by gas injection, summed over all injected species.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous neutral-gas throughput supplied to the vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate. It combines all injected neutral species rather than representing one gas species. For the set of injected species, the equivalent-electron rate is defined by: $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} Z_s\,\dot{N}_s $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the total equivalent-electron source rate, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of injected neutral gas species, $\dot{N}_s$ is the particle injection rate of species $s$, and $Z_s$ is the equivalent-electron weighting per injected particle. For an atomic species, $Z_s$ is its atomic number; for a molecule, it is the sum of the atomic numbers of its constituent atoms. The quantity applies to the vessel-level gas input and is aggregated by summing over all injected neutral species. It is an instantaneous rate, not a time-integrated inventory, and excludes ionization and subsequent plasma particle sources. Species-resolved rates such as the [hydrogen source rate due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) provide individual contributions to this total. Unlike the [total lower gas source rate of the vacuum vessel due to gas injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection), it is not restricted to the lower vessel region. The corresponding accumulated quantity, such as the [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), is obtained by time integration and represents delivered inventory rather than instantaneous throughput.

rows.name: xenon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
rows.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate for xenon atoms supplied by gas injection, assigning 54 equivalent electrons to each xenon atom.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which xenon is supplied by gas injection, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. It represents injected xenon inventory rather than electron production or the xenon content already present in the plasma. The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t) = 54\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t) $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the atomic number of xenon, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the xenon-atom injection rate due to gas injection, and $t$ is time. The quantity applies only to xenon supplied by gas injection and aggregates the injected xenon-atom rate by weighting each atom with xenon's atomic number. It is species-resolved and instantaneous, not a total rate over all injected gasses. The factor 54 is an equivalent-electron bookkeeping convention based on nuclear charge, not a count of free electrons produced by ionization. This rate is distinct from an accumulated xenon inventory; integrating it over time gives the equivalent-electron inventory delivered by gas injection. The same species-resolved convention is used for the [helium-4 gas-injection source rate](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and [hydrogen gas-injection source rate](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

rows.name: field_line_length
rows.description: Arclength of an individually traced magnetic field line during plasma initiation, resolving the field-line length distribution rather than reporting an average connection length.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the geometric arclength of one magnetic field line traced during plasma initiation. It characterizes the distribution of individual field-line lengths associated with the evolving magnetic topology. For a field-line trajectory parameterized by $(s)$, its length is $$ L = \int_{s_0}^{s_1} \left\lVert \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{ds} \right\rVert ds $$ where $L$ is the field-line length, $(s)$ is the position vector along the traced magnetic field line, $s$ is a tracing parameter, and $s_0$ and $s_1$ delimit the traced segment. The quantity applies separately to each traced magnetic field line during the plasma-initiation phase; it is not an average, sum, or charge-state aggregation. It does not impose the open-field-line averaging and closed-line replacement convention of [connection length](name:connection_length), and it is distinct from field-line fraction, which describes the fraction of lines that are open. The set of individual lengths provides a geometric characterization of magnetic topology, while the open-line fraction identifies the prevalence of open field lines within the same traced population.

rows.name: boron_density_at_limiter
rows.description: Boron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral boron atoms.
rows.documentation: Boron density at a limiter is the local number density of boron ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. $$ n_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}=\sum_{q=1}^{5}n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L) $$ where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of counted boron ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the density of boron charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The sum includes boron ions from B$^{+}$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ and excludes neutral boron atoms. This is the boron-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter); unlike [boron density at the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is evaluated specifically at the limiter-side location.

rows.name: electron_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
rows.description: Kinetic-energy power carried away per unit wall area by electrons emitted from a plasma-facing surface after passage through the sheath.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by electrons released from a plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes. It represents energy transported by the emitted electron population after sheath transmission. The emitted electron kinetic-energy flux density is related to the emitted particle flux and the mean kinetic energy per emitted electron by $$ q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}\,\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}} $$ where $q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is this kinetic-energy flux density, $\Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is the [electron particle flux due to surface emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), and $\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}}$ is the mean kinetic energy carried by each emitted electron. The quantity applies specifically to emitted electrons at the wall surface and is aggregated over the emitted electron population, rather than representing an individual electron energy or a spatial maximum. It excludes energy carried by incident electrons, emitted ions, emitted photons, and non-kinetic energy of emitted electrons. It is the electron kinetic contribution to the broader [energy flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), which also includes other emitted energy channels. It is distinct from the incident wall energy represented by energy flux at the wall and from the corresponding emitted-ion quantity [ion kinetic energy flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Sign convention: Positive when kinetic energy is carried away from the wall into the plasma.

rows.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
rows.description: Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission of material from plasma-facing surfaces, weighted by the electron contribution of each emitted species after ionization.
rows.documentation:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission is the rate at which ionization of material released from plasma-facing surfaces adds electrons to the plasma particle balance. It aggregates all emitted fuel, molecular, and impurity species over all plasma-facing surfaces, with each emitted particle weighted by the number of bound electrons it can contribute after full ionization. The global rate is defined by integrating the emitted particle flux density over the plasma-facing surface area: $$ S_e^{\mathrm{surf}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf}}} \sum_s 
u_{e,s}\,\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA $$ where $S_e^{\mathrm{surf}}$ is the electron-equivalent surface-emission source rate, $A_{\mathrm{pf}}$ is the total plasma-facing surface area, $s$ indexes emitted species, $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the emitted particle flux density of species $s$ at surface position $\mathbf{x}$ directed toward the plasma, $dA$ is a surface element, and $
u_{e,s}$ is the electron yield of one emitted particle on full ionization. For an emitted atom, $
u_{e,s}=Z_s$ with $Z_s$ the nuclear charge number; for an emitted molecule or compound particle, $
u_{e,s}$ is the sum of the nuclear charge numbers of its constituent atoms. Surface emission includes recycling, delayed outgassing, and physical or chemical sputtering only insofar as the released material returns toward the plasma and is ionized. This quantity is the electron-specific counterpart of source_rate_due_to_surface_emission, is distinct from externally supplied material represented by [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), excludes electron loss by incidence on surfaces, and contributes to [total_electron_source_rate](name:total_electron_source_rate). Sign convention: Positive when ionization of material emitted from plasma-facing surfaces supplies electron-equivalent particles to the plasma.

rows.name: flux_at_limiter
rows.description: Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. It fixes the limiter locus and the local surface-flux character; more specific quantities state the energy channel being carried, as in energy flux at limiter.
rows.documentation: Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. As a structural parent, it fixes the limiter locus and the local per-area rate character shared by its members, while each more specific name states the particular energy channel being deposited. For a local limiter surface element, the flux is the rate of the deposited quantity per surface area: $$ q_{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\partial^2 Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}}{\partial A_{\mathrm{lim}}\,\partial t} $$ where $q_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the flux at limiter, $Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}$ is the energy-dimensioned quantity delivered by the plasma to the limiter surface element, $A_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the area of that limiter plasma-facing surface element, and $t$ is time. The scope is restricted to plasma-facing limiter surfaces, and the quantity is local to the surface element: it carries no built-in integration, maximum, average, or other aggregation over the limiter unless a more specific standard name states such an aggregation. The carried quantity always has the dimension of energy, so every member of this family shares the same surface power-density character; the family does not extend to particle-count or momentum surface fluxes, which are dimensionally distinct quantities. This quantity excludes fluxes to non-limiter wall components, the total power deposited on a limiter, and signed vector heat-flux components normal to a surface. The more specific [energy flux at limiter](name:energy_flux_at_limiter) is the attested member that fixes the carried quantity as plasma energy deposition, inheriting the local limiter-surface rate-density semantics defined here.

rows.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall
rows.description: Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated arrival rate of neutral particles of one specified species moving from the plasma side toward plasma-facing material. It excludes neutral particles emitted by the wall.
rows.documentation: Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated rate at which neutral particles of one specified species arrive at plasma-facing material from the plasma side. It counts incoming neutral particles crossing the material boundary toward the wall, not particles emitted by the wall. The wall-integrated arrival rate is the surface integral of the corresponding local incident flux: $$ \dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_\mathrm{wall}} \Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})\, dA $$ where $\dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ denotes this incident neutral particle flux at the wall, $A_\mathrm{wall}$ is the plasma-facing wall surface included in the total, $\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the incident component of the local neutral particle flux at the wall for the same neutral species at wall position $\mathbf{x}$, and $dA$ is the surface-area element. The quantity is species-resolved for one neutral species and aggregated over wall position by surface integration. It is not the local per-area neutral particle flux at the wall at a given wall position, and it is not a signed net balance between incoming and outgoing neutrals. Wall-emitted neutral particles belong to the opposite direction of exchange and are represented separately by quantities such as [neutral particle flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Contributions from disjoint wall regions add to form the global incident rate.

rows.name: kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
rows.description: Kinetic-energy power flux density carried away from a plasma-facing surface by emitted particles, including ions and electrons and aggregated over species.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by particles emitted from a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, secondary emission, or related surface-emission processes. It includes all emitted particle species and charge states, rather than selecting a particular ion or charge state. The kinetic-energy flux density is defined by $$ q_{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $s$ indexes emitted particle species and charge states, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m/s, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is the emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes particles incident on the surface. This is the kinetic component of [energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), excluding particle potential-energy contributions and photon or other radiative energy; [ion charge-state kinetic energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) is a charge-state-resolved instance.

rows.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall
rows.description: Incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state as they arrive at a plasma-facing wall.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state as they cross onto a plasma-facing wall. It includes only translational kinetic energy and only particles moving from the plasma toward the wall. $$ q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\left(-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ Here $q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy flux density, $s$ identifies the internal quantum state, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity relative to the wall, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ is the unit normal directed from the wall toward the plasma, and $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that state. Unlike [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall), this quantity weights arrivals by translational kinetic energy; neutral_energy_flux_at_wall aggregates the corresponding kinetic-energy flux over internal states. Internal excitation, potential, and rest-mass energies are excluded.

rows.name: power_at_wall_due_to_convection
rows.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
rows.documentation: Convective power at plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces quantifies the energy transported by bulk plasma-particle flow from the scrape-off layer into the material surfaces. It comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions and is the surface-integrated component of [power due to convection](name:power_due_to_convection). $$ P_{\mathrm{conv,wall}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} q_{\mathrm{conv}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}A $$ where $P_{\mathrm{conv,wall}}$ is the total convective power, $q_{\mathrm{conv}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local convective energy flux density at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the combined plasma-facing wall and divertor surface area included in the quantity. Only convective particle-energy transport is included; conductive and radiative deposition are excluded. [Power at a single divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection) isolates one target, while [convective power summed over divertor targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection) includes only the divertor-target subset. The conductive counterpart is [power at the wall due to conduction](name:power_at_wall_due_to_conduction).

rows.name: ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density
rows.description: Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to local free-electron number density.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the local iron-to-electron abundance ratio in a plasma, comparing the population of iron ions with unbound free electrons. $$ R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e} $$ where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total [iron-ion number density](name:iron_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density). The numerator is summed over all positive iron ionization states, while the denominator counts free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions. This is a local ratio with no volume averaging, maximum operation, or specified spatial locus. The ratio is the iron-specific counterpart of the general [ion-density-to-electron-density ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density); its numerator is the charge-state-summed iron density and its denominator is the electron-density parent quantity.

rows.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
rows.description: Dimensionless global boron abundance ratio using separately volume-averaged boron and electron number densities, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the global abundance of elemental boron relative to the electron population. It characterizes plasma composition over the full plasma volume rather than at a local point or along a line of sight. The defining ratio is $$ f_B = \frac{\overline{n}_B}{\overline{n}_e} $$ where $f_B$ is the boron-to-electron abundance ratio, $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged elemental boron number density, and $\overline{n}_e$ is the volume-averaged electron number density. The overbar denotes averaging over the plasma volume. The numerator includes neutral boron and every ionic boron charge state, while the denominator represents the complete electron population. For the associated plasma-composition convention, the ratio is evaluated at the time of peak electron density. This quantity is distinct from local [boron density](name:boron_density) and from [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density): it is a quotient of two separately volume-averaged densities, not a volume average of a pointwise ratio or a line average. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), making this ratio the corresponding normalized composition measure.

rows.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_oxygen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
rows.description: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density for the plasma, with oxygen summed over ionized charge states and neutral oxygen excluded.
rows.documentation: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density is a scalar oxygen impurity fraction for the plasma. It compares the charge-state-summed volume average of ionized oxygen number density with the corresponding volume average of electron number density over the same averaging volume. The ratio is defined by $$ f_O = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{O^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V} $$ where $f_O$ is this oxygen-to-electron density ratio, $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes a volume average over the averaging volume $V$, $q$ is the oxygen charge-state index, $n_{O^{q+}}$ is the local number density of oxygen ions in charge state $q+$, and $n_e$ is the local electron number density. The denominator $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The numerator is summed over ionized oxygen charge states $O^{1+}$ through $O^{8+}$ and excludes neutral oxygen. This quantity is a single scalar composition fraction formed from volume-averaged populations; it is distinct from a local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), from a [line-averaged oxygen density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), and from a neutral-inclusive [volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) when that quantity includes neutral oxygen. The essential relationship is normalization: the charge-state-summed volume-averaged oxygen ion density is divided by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), so the result represents oxygen ion abundance relative to the electron population rather than an absolute density.

rows.name: surface_emissivity
rows.description: Dimensionless ratio of thermal radiation emitted by a surface to blackbody radiation at the same surface temperature, with the stated spectral and angular averaging.
rows.documentation: Surface emissivity is the effectiveness of a material surface in emitting thermal electromagnetic radiation relative to an ideal blackbody at the same temperature. It is a material property of the emitting surface and is distinct from the emitted energy flux described by [energy flux due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). The effective emissivity is defined by $$ \varepsilon = \frac{M_{\mathrm{emit}}(T_s)}{M_{\mathrm{bb}}(T_s)} $$ where $M_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface thermal radiative exitance, $M_{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the blackbody exitance, and $T_s$ is the surface temperature. The ratio applies to the specified spectral band and angular averaging; it is not a wavelength- and direction-resolved emissivity. Incident radiation and geometric surface area, such as optical-element area, are excluded.

rows.name: y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
rows.description: Signed y coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture in the right-handed camera Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the signed Cartesian y coordinate of a diagnostic aperture's geometric center, measured from the origin of the right-handed camera basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It locates the aperture along the camera-frame y axis. The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position vector: $$ y_{\rm ap} = \mathbf{r}_{\rm ap} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}} $$ where $y_{\rm ap}$ is the coordinate value, $\mathbf{r}_{\rm ap}$ is the aperture-center position relative to the camera-frame origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector; the length quantities are expressed in m. This camera-frame coordinate is distinct from the radial and vertical coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Together with the [x coordinate of the diagnostic aperture](name:x_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture), it locates the aperture center in the camera frame. Sign convention: Positive when the aperture center lies in the positive y direction from the camera-frame origin.

rows.name: y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera
rows.description: Y-axis component of a camera’s image-up orientation unit vector, expressed in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
rows.documentation: The camera image-up unit vector specifies the orientation of increasing image-up direction, distinct from the camera line-of-sight direction. This quantity is its projection onto the Cartesian y-axis. $$ u_{\mathrm{up},y} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}} $$ where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}}$ is the image-up orientation unit vector and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-axis unit vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The complete image-up vector has unit magnitude, so its components satisfy $u_{\mathrm{up},x}^2 + u_{\mathrm{up},y}^2 + u_{\mathrm{up},z}^2 = 1$. This component is distinct from the camera line-of-sight components represented by [x-direction unit vector of camera](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-direction unit vector of camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

rows.name: bremsstrahlung_power
rows.description: Total electromagnetic power emitted by free-free bremsstrahlung as electrons accelerate in the Coulomb fields of plasma ions.
rows.documentation: Bremsstrahlung power is the total electromagnetic power emitted by free-free radiation from electron acceleration in the Coulomb fields of plasma ions. It is integrated over the emitting plasma volume and the full photon-frequency range. $$ P_{\mathrm{brem}} = \int_V \int_0^\infty \varepsilon_{\mathrm{brem}}(\mathbf{x},\omega)\,d\omega\,d^3\mathbf{x} $$ where $P_{\mathrm{brem}}$ is the total bremsstrahlung power, $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\omega$ is photon angular frequency, and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{brem}}$ is the spectral volumetric bremsstrahlung emissivity. This quantity is a contribution to [total plasma radiated power](name:total_plasma_radiated_power) and excludes discrete [line radiation](name:power_due_to_line_radiation) and [synchrotron radiation](name:power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation).

rows.name: cold_neutral_velocity
rows.description: Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk flow of low-energy neutral atoms, identified from the Doppler shift of their emission.
rows.documentation: Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk drift vector of a cold neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing cold-neutral population states. The component is defined from the parent [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) by $$ v_{n,c,ell} = \mathbf{v}_{n,c} \cdot \hat{\ell} $$ where $\mathbf{v}_{n,c}$ is the bulk velocity of the cold neutral population, $\hat{\ell}$ is the selected line-of-sight unit vector, and $v_{n,c,\ell}$ is the signed projected velocity. The projection is the velocity represented by the Doppler centroid of the corresponding cold-neutral emission component. This quantity is distinct from [hot neutral velocity](name:hot_neutral_velocity), which describes the energetic neutral population, and from [neutral internal state velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity), which is resolved for a specified internal state. It excludes thermal speed and velocity spread, which are higher moments of the velocity distribution. Sign convention: Positive when the cold-neutral bulk velocity points along the chosen positive line-of-sight unit vector $\hat{\ell}$.

rows.name: deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion
rows.description: Local volumetric rate of neutron production from deuterium-deuterium fusion reactions, giving the spatial distribution of D-D neutron emission per unit volume at each point in the plasma.
rows.documentation: The deuterium-deuterium neutron emissivity $\varepsilon_{DD}$ is the local number of neutrons produced per unit volume per unit time from D-D fusion reactions. Only the neutron-emitting D-D branch contributes, so this quantity is the local source of prompt fusion neutrons from deuterium-deuterium reactions that produce a neutron. For identical deuterium reactants, the branch emissivity is given by: $$ \varepsilon_{DD} = \frac{1}{2} n_D^2 \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DD,n} $$ where $\varepsilon_{DD}$ is the deuterium-deuterium neutron emissivity, $n_D$ is the local deuterium reactant number density, $\sigma$ is the fusion cross-section for the neutron-emitting D-D branch, $v$ is the relative speed of the deuterium reactants, and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DD,n}$ is the velocity average of $\sigma v$ over the local reactant distributions. The factor $1/2$ avoids double-counting unordered pairs of identical deuterium reactants. The scope is the D-D reaction channel at a plasma location, aggregated over all deuterium reactant charge states and kinetic populations that contribute to the local neutron-emitting D-D branch unless a component-resolved quantity is specified. It excludes the proton-emitting D-D branch, subsequent D-T neutron production involving tritium born from D-D reactions, and the [deuterium-tritium neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion). The reaction-pair label deuterium_deuterium denotes two deuterium reactants; it is not a charge-state-resolved fuel-state quantity. Integrating $\varepsilon_{DD}$ over a plasma volume gives the D-D contribution to the global neutron flux for the same reactant population, and weighting that contribution by the branch neutron energy gives its contribution to total neutron power. When reactant populations are resolved, the corresponding global neutron production can be decomposed into [thermal neutron flux](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion), beam-thermal neutron flux, and beam-beam neutron flux contributions; those are population decompositions of the volume-integrated source, not separate definitions of the local D-D emissivity. Together with [deuterium-tritium neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion), this quantity is a reaction-channel-specific member of [neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:neutron_emissivity_due_to_fusion).

rows.name: energy_of_detector_pixel
rows.description: The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is distinct from the lower and upper bandpass-edge energies.
rows.documentation: The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is the energy counterpart of the [wavelength of detector pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel) and identifies the pixel's spectral-channel assignment rather than the finite width of its accepted band. For diffraction order $n$, the representative pixel energy is related to the pixel Bragg angle by Bragg's law and the photon energy-wavelength relation: $$ E_\mathrm{pix} = \frac{n h c}{2 e d \sin\theta_\mathrm{pix}} $$ where $E_\mathrm{pix}$ is the energy of the detector pixel, $n$ is the diffraction order, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $d$ is the spacing of the diffracting crystal planes, and $\theta_\mathrm{pix}$ is the Bragg angle associated with the pixel. This representative energy is the calibrated spectral-channel value selected by the spectrometer energy scale; it need not equal the arithmetic midpoint between the [lower bound energy of detector pixel](name:lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel) and the [upper bound energy of detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which define the edges of the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

rows.name: etendue_of_hard_xray_detector
rows.description: Geometric optical throughput of a hard X-ray detector’s optical system, determined by its effective collecting area and accepted solid angle.
rows.documentation: Étendue is the geometric throughput of the optical system associated with a hard X-ray detector. It characterizes the angular and spatial acceptance that determines how incident radiation is coupled into the detector. The defining relation is $$ G = A\Omega $$ where $G$ is the detector étendue, $A$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega$ is the accepted solid angle. This quantity applies to the detector-level optical system and uses effective area and angular acceptance for the associated detector; it does not specify whether those properties arise from one or multiple optical elements. It is distinct from the detector’s linear dimensions, such as its [height](name:height_of_hard_xray_detector) and width, which do not determine optical throughput alone. Étendue provides the geometric factor relating incident [hard X-ray brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness) to radiation coupled into the detector and is the same physical optical-throughput concept represented by [etendue_of_spectrometer](name:etendue_of_spectrometer), with the owning optical system changed from a spectrometer to a hard X-ray detector.

rows.name: extent_of_soft_xray_detector
rows.description: Full end-to-end physical size of a soft X-ray detector along the applicable horizontal or vertical detector-plane direction.
rows.documentation: The detector extent is the complete end-to-end linear size of the soft X-ray detector along one specified detector-plane direction. It characterizes the physical detector boundary rather than a spectral or radiometric property. For a coordinate $s$ measured along the selected detector-plane direction, the extent $L$ is defined by $$ L = s_{\max} - s_{\min} $$ where $s_{\max}$ and $s_{\min}$ are the coordinates of the two opposite physical boundaries. The applicable direction is horizontal or vertical within the detector plane. This quantity describes an overall detector dimension and is distinct from pixel dimensions, collecting [area of a diagnostic aperture](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture), and optical throughput such as the [étendue of a hard X-ray detector](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector).

rows.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
rows.description: Signed coordinate of a soft X-ray detector outline vertex along the first local tangential (X1) axis of the detector-local two-dimensional Cartesian frame.
rows.documentation: The first local tangential coordinate specifies the signed displacement of an outline vertex along the first tangential axis (X1) of the detector-local Cartesian frame. Together with [second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector), it defines the polygonal boundary of the soft X-ray detector's sensitive area projected onto the object-local plane. The two coordinates $(X_1, X_2)$ form a right-handed pair intrinsic to the owning detector object; their orientation is fixed per detector installation and is not in general aligned with the machine cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement is in the direction of the positive first local tangential axis of the detector-local frame.

rows.name: hard_xray_brightness
rows.description: Band-integrated hard X-ray photon radiance received by a channel, normalized by projected collecting area and accepted solid angle.
rows.documentation: Hard X-ray brightness is the photon radiance received from a viewing direction by a channel. It represents photon arrival rate with the photon-energy dependence integrated over the selected hard X-ray band. The band-integrated photon radiance is defined by $$ B_{\mathrm{HX}} = \frac{dN_\gamma}{dt\,dA_{\mathrm{proj}}\,d\Omega} $$ where $B_{\mathrm{HX}}$ is the hard X-ray brightness, $N_\gamma$ is the number of received photons in the selected energy band, $t$ is time, $A_{\mathrm{proj}}$ is projected collecting area, and $\Omega$ is accepted solid angle. This quantity applies to hard X-ray photons received by a channel and is evaluated separately for each selected energy band. Its aggregation convention is integration over photon energy within that band while retaining normalization by projected area and solid angle. It is a received radiometric quantity, not a local volumetric source term, and it counts photons rather than their deposited or carried energy. The local production counterpart is hard X-ray emissivity, which describes photon generation per unit volume and solid angle before propagation to the channel. Integrating this brightness over the collecting geometry represented by the [etendue of a hard X-ray detector](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector) gives the received photon rate under the corresponding angular and area acceptance. Unlike [incident soft X-ray radiance](name:incident_soft_xray_radiance), which is energy-weighted, this quantity is photon-count radiance; photon registration probability is a separate detector property described by [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector).

rows.name: height_of_hard_xray_detector
rows.description: Height of a hard X-ray detector is the full edge-to-edge extent of its rectangular aperture along the second local tangential axis, X2, in the local Cartesian (X1, X2, X3) frame.
rows.documentation: Height of hard xray detector It applies to a rectangular detector aperture and denotes a full extent, not a half-extent, signed coordinate, detector location, housing dimension, or extent along the local normal. It is distinct from the extent of a separate channel collimating aperture and from the first local tangential extent, represented by the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector). For a rectangular detector aperture, this height and the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector) are its two orthogonal in-plane full dimensions; together they determine the aperture opening area. That area contributes to the [hard X-ray detector etendue](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector), which also depends on the accepted solid angle.

rows.name: lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel
rows.description: The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy accepted by that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
rows.documentation: The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy at the low-energy edge of the spectral interval accepted by an individual detector pixel in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It defines the lower endpoint of that pixel's photon-energy acceptance range. This quantity applies to photons assigned to one detector pixel and represents a per-pixel spectral-channel boundary, not an integrated or averaged energy over multiple pixels or channels. It is distinct from the [energy of a detector pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which is the central or representative photon energy assigned to the pixel, and from the [upper bound energy of a detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which defines the high-energy edge. Together, the lower and upper bounds delimit the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

rows.name: outer_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak
rows.description: Outward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak from its maximum to the outer half-maximum point toward the separatrix in normalized toroidal flux.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the outward half-width of the hard X-ray emissivity peak, measured from the emissivity maximum toward the separatrix in normalized toroidal flux. It characterizes the radial spread of hard X-ray emission associated with nonthermal electrons on the outer side of the peak. $$ h_{\mathrm{outer}} = \rho_{\mathrm{half,out}} - \rho_{\mathrm{peak}}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}(\rho_{\mathrm{half,out}}) = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}(\rho_{\mathrm{peak}}) $$ Here, $h_{\mathrm{outer}}$ is the outward half-width, $\rho_{\mathrm{peak}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate of the hard X-ray emissivity maximum, $\rho_{\mathrm{half,out}}$ is the outer coordinate where the emissivity reaches half its peak value, and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}$ is the hard X-ray emissivity as a function of normalized toroidal-flux coordinate $\rho$. The quantity applies only to the outer side of the emissivity peak, with increasing $\rho$ directed toward the separatrix. It is a nonnegative extent and is distinct from the inward half-width, which measures the corresponding distance on the magnetic-axis side of the peak. Together, the two directional widths characterize the asymmetric spread of the peak; the [inner hard X-ray half-width at the emissivity peak](name:inner_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak) provides the inward counterpart.

rows.name: power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation
rows.description: Total electromagnetic power emitted by relativistic electrons as synchrotron radiation while their gyromotion is curved by the plasma magnetic field.
rows.documentation: Power due to synchrotron radiation is the total electromagnetic power emitted by relativistic electrons as synchrotron radiation while their gyromotion is curved by the plasma magnetic field. It is a mechanism-specific contribution to the plasma radiative power and refers to emitted radiation, not stored electromagnetic energy. For an emitting plasma volume $V$, the quantity is defined by the volume integral of the local synchrotron volumetric emissivity: $$ P_{\mathrm{syn}} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{syn}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{syn}}$ is the power due to synchrotron radiation, $p_{\mathrm{syn}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local synchrotron volumetric emissivity formed from the relativistic electron phase-space distribution and the local magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, and $dV$ is a volume element. This quantity includes only synchrotron emission and excludes [bremsstrahlung power](name:bremsstrahlung_power) and [power due to line radiation](name:power_due_to_line_radiation). It denotes gross electromagnetic power emitted by the radiating electrons and is distinct from net synchrotron power escaping a plasma-facing or material boundary after reabsorption or reflection.

rows.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal
rows.description: Signed coordinate of a Bragg-crystal outline vertex along the second local tangential axis of the crystal-local Cartesian (X1, X2) frame.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the signed position of a vertex on the Bragg-crystal outline, resolved along the crystal-local second tangential direction. It describes the crystal geometry in the local planar Cartesian frame $(X_1, X_2)$ rather than in the machine cylindrical frame. For a vertex position vector $\mathbf{r}$ and local-frame origin $\mathbf{r}_0$, the coordinate is defined by: $$ x_2 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 $$ where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the unit vector along the second local tangential axis, and $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the crystal-local frame. Together with the [first local tangential coordinate of the Bragg crystal](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal), it specifies the in-plane location of the outline vertex. Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the crystal-local origin has a positive projection along the second local tangential unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$.

rows.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_optical_element
rows.description: Signed position of a fiber center or outline vertex at an optical element along its second local tangential axis, measured relative to the element-local origin.
rows.documentation: The second local tangential coordinate locates an individual fiber center or outline vertex at an optical element. It belongs to the element-local Cartesian frame $(X_1, X_2)$, where $X_1$ and $X_2$ denote coordinates along the first and second local tangents, respectively. The coordinate is defined by $$ X_2 = (\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_0)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2 $$ where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of the specified point, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the position vector of the element-local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2$ is the unit vector along the positive second local tangent. Each value describes one fiber center or outline vertex, not an average over those points. Fiber-center coordinates locate individual fibers, whereas outline coordinates locate boundary vertices; neither denotes an element width or a surface-normal displacement. The second tangent is object-local and is not prescribed to be vertical. For fiber-center positions in a fiber bundle, the [first local tangential coordinate of the fiber bundle] supplies the complementary coordinate of the same center in the local plane. Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the element-local origin has a positive projection onto the designated second local tangential axis.

rows.name: spectral_wavelength_of_optical_element
rows.description: Wavelength at an optical element specifies the vacuum spectral position at which its transmission, absorption, or other wavelength-dependent optical properties are evaluated.
rows.documentation: Wavelength of optical element The defining relation is $$ \lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} $$ where $\lambda$ is the vacuum wavelength, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, and $\nu$ is the radiation frequency. Each value denotes a spectral evaluation point, not a response amplitude or wavelength interval. It does not inherently designate a passband center or edge, and it denotes the vacuum wavelength rather than the wavelength within the element's material. The definition is not restricted to a particular spectral band. The [spectral refractive index of an optical element](name:spectral_refractive_index_of_optical_element) and, for a filter, the [spectral absorptivity](name:spectral_absorptivity_of_filter) are response quantities evaluated as functions of this wavelength.

rows.name: toroidal_angular_width_of_camera
rows.description: Full angular span of a camera field of view in the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, equal to the non-negative difference between the largest and smallest unwrapped toroidal viewing angles.
rows.documentation: Full angular span of a camera field of view in the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is the non-negative difference between the largest and smallest limiting signed toroidal viewing angles subtended by the camera acceptance. In this frame $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. Let $\phi_{\min}$ and $\phi_{\max}$ be the minimum and maximum unwrapped signed toroidal viewing angles of the limiting accepted rays. The toroidal angular width is defined by: $$ \Delta\phi_\mathrm{cam} = \phi_{\max} - \phi_{\min} $$ where $\Delta\phi_\mathrm{cam}$ is the toroidal angular width of the camera and the extrema are taken over the camera field-of-view boundary after choosing a continuous branch of $\phi$. This quantity describes only the toroidal extent of the field of view. It excludes the central toroidal pointing angle, the detailed field-of-view footprint or optical distortion, and the complementary [vertical angular width](name:vertical_angular_width_of_camera).

rows.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_reflector
rows.description: Toroidal angular coordinate of the center of the sphere defining a reflector’s spherical mirror surface, locating that center around the symmetry axis.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal angle of the center of the sphere that defines a reflector’s spherical mirror surface. It identifies the reflector-center azimuth, not the mirror’s angular extent, orientation, or curvature. The toroidal angle $[?25l\phi_c$ of the sphere center is defined from its projection onto the horizontal plane: $$ \phi_c = \operatorname{atan2}(y_c,x_c) $$ where $x_c$ and $y_c$ are the center coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. Equivalently, $\phi_c$ is the angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Its geometric meaning parallels [toroidal coordinate of an optical element](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_optical_element), but the locus here is the reflector sphere center. Sign convention: Positive when the angle is measured in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

rows.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
rows.description: Toroidal angle of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal coordinate of the geometric center of a soft X-ray detector. The center is the detector geometry reference point, including the center of a circular detector or the origin of its local detector coordinate system. The toroidal angle is defined from the detector-center Cartesian coordinates: $$ \phi_{\rm det} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_{\rm det}, x_{\rm det}) $$ where $x_{\rm det}$ and $y_{\rm det}$ are the Cartesian coordinate values of the detector center in the right-handed $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. The corresponding vertical location is given by the [vertical coordinate of the soft X-ray detector](name:vertical_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector). Sign convention: Positive when the detector center lies in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: tritium_density
rows.description: Local number density of tritium ions in the plasma, the foundational fuel-ion parameter underlying chord-averaged, volume-averaged, and isotopic ratio child quantities.
rows.documentation: Tritium ion number density $n_T$ quantifies the local concentration of hydrogen-3 fuel ions in the plasma. It serves as the common physical basis for a family of derived quantities: the chord-integrated mean [line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density), the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), and dimensionless isotopic ratios such as ratio_of_tritium_density_to_electron_density and [ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density). In deuterium-tritium (DT) fusion plasmas the local volumetric reaction rate is: $$ R_{DT} = n_T \, n_D \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT} $$ where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}$ is the Maxwellian-averaged DT fusion reactivity. The combined DT fuel-ion purity relative to the electron population is tracked by ratio_of_deuterium_tritium_density_to_electron_density. Tritium density is inferred from active charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, neutron emission measurements in DT plasmas, or pellet injection and fueling diagnostics.

rows.name: runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density
rows.description: Kinetic energy per unit volume carried by the runaway-electron population, including relativistic motion and excluding rest-mass energy.
rows.documentation: Number density of runaway electron The local kinetic energy density is defined by: $$ w_{\mathrm{RE}} = n_{\mathrm{RE}}\left\langle (\gamma-1)m_e c^2 \right\rangle_{\mathrm{RE}} $$ where $w_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron kinetic energy density, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{RE}}$ denotes a particle-number-weighted average over the local runaway-electron population. The Lorentz factor is $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, where $v$ is electron speed, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, and $c$ is the speed of light. Only the runaway-electron population is included, not the bulk thermal-electron population. The energy includes motion both parallel and perpendicular to the magnetic field but excludes rest-mass energy and electromagnetic-field energy. For a magnetic-flux-surface description, the quantity is the mean of the local energy density over each magnetic flux surface, not a mean over the entire confined plasma volume. It is an energy per volume, not a mean energy per electron. Its plasma-volume integral is the total [runaway-electron kinetic energy](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy), denoted $W_{\mathrm{RE}}$. Dividing that integral by the same plasma volume gives the [volume-averaged runaway-electron kinetic energy density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density).

rows.name: volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate
rows.description: Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons, summed over Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay generation mechanisms.
rows.documentation: Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons is the spatial average, over the plasma volume, of the local total rate at which electrons enter the runaway population. The total rate includes generation by Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay mechanisms. The volume average is defined by $$ \left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V = \frac{1}{|\Omega_p|}\int_{\Omega_p} S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $\left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged total runaway electron source rate, $S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total runaway electron source rate at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega_p$ is the plasma-volume domain, $|\Omega_p|$ is the volume measure of that domain, and $dV$ is the volume element. This quantity applies to the runaway-electron population within the plasma volume and uses an unweighted volume average of the total local volumetric production rate. The mechanism sum is part of the quantity definition; the total includes component production rates such as the [Dreicer runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer) and the [hot-tail runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), but is not restricted to either component. It is the plasma-volume-averaged counterpart of the total runaway electron source rate. It is a production-rate density averaged over volume, not the absolute number of runaway electrons and not a current-density measure; in particular it is distinct from the [volume-averaged parallel runaway electron current density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), which describes charge transport by the runaway population.

rows.name: focal_length_of_line_of_sight
rows.description: Paraxial focal length of the collector optics associated with a charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight, setting the distance from the principal plane to the focal point.
rows.documentation: The focal length is the paraxial distance from the principal plane of the collector optical system to the focal point for collimated incident rays. It characterizes the focusing geometry associated with a selected charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight. This quantity applies to the collector optics of that line of sight and is not the diameter of the focused image spot or the optical throughput. The diameter of the line of sight describes the focused spot size, while the [etendue of the line of sight](name:etendue_of_line_of_sight) describes its accepted optical phase space; both are related to, but distinct from, focal length.

rows.name: radius_of_detector
rows.description: Radius from the center to the circumferential edge of a detector's circular front face, defining its geometric size for optical throughput.
rows.documentation: The detector radius is the geometric distance from the center of a circular detector front face to its circumferential edge. The corresponding circular face area is defined by $$ A_{\rm det} = \pi r_{\rm det}^{2} $$ where $A_{\rm det}$ is the detector front-face area, $r_{\rm det}$ is the detector radius, and $\pi$ is the mathematical constant. This quantity applies only when the detector front face has circular geometry. It describes the detector face itself and does not represent a collimating aperture, a filter opening, or a width parameter for a noncircular detector geometry. The face area determined by this radius contributes to the geometric optical throughput represented by [spectrometer etendue](name:etendue_of_spectrometer); it is distinct from the radius of a separate [spectrometer aperture](name:radius_of_aperture).

rows.name: radius_of_reflector
rows.description: Geometric distance from the center of a reflector’s circular aperture to its circumferential boundary in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
rows.documentation: The reflector aperture radius is the geometric distance from the center of the circular opening to its circumferential boundary. It defines the circular cross-section of the optical reflector through which light is directed toward the crystal. For a circular aperture, its area is related to the radius by $$ A = \pi r^2 $$ where $A$ is the aperture area, $r$ is the reflector aperture radius, and $\pi$ is the mathematical constant relating a circle’s circumference to its diameter. This quantity applies only to a reflector with circular aperture geometry. It describes the aperture radius, not a curvature radius of the reflector surface or the radius of a different optical element. The same geometric concept is used for the circular Bragg-crystal opening represented by [radius of Bragg crystal](name:radius_of_bragg_crystal), while [radius of aperture](name:radius_of_aperture) describes a channel-level collimating aperture rather than the reflector aperture.

rows.name: surface_area_of_detector
rows.description: Geometric surface area of the detector face defining the physical extent of one diagnostic detector.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the geometric area of the specified detector surface associated with one diagnostic channel. It characterizes the physical extent of that detector surface as defined by its boundary and geometry. The surface area is defined by $$ A_{\mathrm{det}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{det}}} dA $$ where $A_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector surface area, $S_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the specified detector surface, and $dA$ is the differential surface-area element. The quantity applies to one detector and is not an aggregate over multiple channels or diagnostic components. It describes geometric surface extent, not a radiation or particle flux, detector response, or sensitivity. The detector surface is distinct from the designated diagnostic aperture described by [area of diagnostic aperture](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture), even when the two geometric surfaces coincide. It follows the same surface-area concept as [surface area of neutron detector](name:surface_area_of_neutron_detector), but is associated with the specified detector rather than specifically with a neutron-sensitive detector.

rows.name: vertical_coordinate_of_polarizer
rows.description: Vertical coordinate of a polarizer is the signed Z position of the polarizer geometric center in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: Vertical coordinate of a polarizer is the $Z$ coordinate of the polarizer geometric center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coordinate is the vertical component of the position of that center: $$ z_{\mathrm{pol}} = Z(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{pol}}) $$ where $z_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the polarizer and $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the position vector of the polarizer geometric center. This quantity applies to the polarizer element itself and only to its geometric center. It is not a vertical extent, surface normal component, orientation angle, or local tangential coordinate of the polarizer. Together with the [radial coordinate of a polarizer](name:radial_coordinate_of_polarizer) and [toroidal coordinate of a polarizer](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_polarizer), it specifies the polarizer center position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Sign convention: Positive when the polarizer geometric center lies in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction from the vertical origin.

rows.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_limiter_tile
rows.description: Nuclear heating power of a limiter tile is the rate at which nuclear energy is deposited within one limiter tile by neutron interactions and associated primary and secondary gamma-ray absorption.
rows.documentation: Nuclear heating power of a limiter tile is the rate at which nuclear energy is deposited within one limiter tile by nuclear radiation transport and interactions in the tile material. It is a scalar heating-power contribution assigned to the material volume of that tile. The volume-integrated relation to the local nuclear power density is $$ P_{\mathrm{nuc},t} = \int_{V_t} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{nuc},t}$ is the nuclear heating power of the limiter tile, $V_t$ is the material volume occupied by the limiter tile, $q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [nuclear power density of the limiter tile](name:nuclear_power_density_of_limiter_tile) at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, and $dV$ is the differential volume element. The quantity applies to a single limiter tile and is aggregated over the whole material volume of that tile.
