It specializes the internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient); it is distinct from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Sign convention: Positive when a negative radial temperature derivative produces a diffusive thermal-energy flux in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity
rows.description: Signed major-radius projection of the mean translational velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the major-radius component of the [neutral internal-state velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity) of one neutral species in one specified quantum or energy state. It represents directed bulk motion after averaging over particle velocities within that state. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by: $$ u_{0,a,R}=\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{R})f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{0,a,R}$ is the major-radius velocity component, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved bulk velocity vector, $0$ identifies neutral particles, and $a$ identifies the specified internal state. The function $f_{0,a}$ is the phase-space number density of the selected neutral species in that state, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The coordinate $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The average retains internal-state resolution and does not combine different states or neutral species. It is a signed vector projection, not the flow speed, thermal velocity spread, or particle flux. The major-radius direction need not coincide with the magnetic-flux-surface normal. The corresponding [radial neutral velocity](name:radial_neutral_velocity) combines internal-state contributions through a number-density-weighted mean; this quantity retains the contribution of the specified state. Sign convention: Positive when the state-resolved neutral bulk motion has a component away from the toroidal symmetry axis, toward increasing major radius.

rows.name: runaway_electron_density
rows.description: Number density of runaway electrons, the suprathermal electron population for which electric-field acceleration can overcome collisional drag.
rows.documentation: Number density of runaway electron The local density is the zeroth momentum-space moment of the runaway-electron distribution: $$ n_{e,\mathrm{RE}} = \int f_{e,\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{p})\,\mathrm{d}^3p $$ where $n_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, $\mathbf{p}$ is electron momentum, and $f_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron momentum distribution at the same spatial position and time. The integral covers all momenta represented in that population. Thermal electrons and suprathermal electrons outside the runaway population are excluded. No orbit-class restriction or spatial averaging is implicit. Unlike [runaway-electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density), this quantity counts particles without weighting them by charge and velocity. The [volume-averaged runaway-electron density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density) is the integral of this local density over the confined plasma volume divided by that volume. The [volume-integrated runaway-electron density](name:volume_integrated_runaway_electron_density) is the integral itself and represents the total runaway-electron count rather than a number density.

rows.name: runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail
rows.description: Hot-tail runaway-electron source rate is the production of runaway electrons per unit volume and time from a suprathermal tail surviving rapid cooling of the bulk electrons.
rows.documentation: Hot-tail runaway-electron source rate quantifies production of runaway electrons from the high-energy electron tail that survives rapid cooling of the bulk population. These tail electrons relax collisionally more slowly than the bulk cools, allowing some to enter the regime where electric-field acceleration overcomes collisional drag. The hot-tail contribution to runaway-electron density evolution is defined by $$ S_{\mathrm{ht}} = \left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{RE}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{hot\text{-}tail}} $$ where $S_{\mathrm{ht}}$ is the volumetric hot-tail production rate, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the [runaway-electron number density](name:runaway_electron_density), and $t$ is time. The restriction on the derivative selects only production through the hot-tail mechanism. This source counts electrons entering the runaway population, not all suprathermal electrons. It excludes generation through other mechanisms, transport, and losses, so it is not the full time derivative of runaway-electron density. It contributes to the [total runaway-electron source rate](name:total_runaway_electron_source_rate), which sums all active generation mechanisms. The [volume-averaged hot-tail runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail) is this same volumetric source integrated over the plasma volume and divided by that volume.

rows.name: suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
rows.description: Kinetic pressure contributed by suprathermal neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, including anisotropic velocity-space contributions from the nonthermal population.
rows.documentation: Suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure is the state-resolved anisotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state. It is a partial pressure for the selected internal state and suprathermal population, not a sum over all internal states and not the thermal neutral contribution. For state $a$, the pressure tensor of the suprathermal population is the central second velocity-space moment: $$ \mathbf{P}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a = m_a \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of suprathermal neutrals in state $a$, $\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a$ is the mean velocity of that selected population, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product. The central moment excludes dynamic pressure from directed bulk flow. Directional or gyrotropic components are projections or averages of this tensor; for example, [perpendicular suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the component transverse to the local magnetic field. [Thermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the corresponding thermal contribution, while [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) combines thermal and suprathermal contributions for the same internal state.

rows.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
rows.description: Effective velocity for convective transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the effective velocity associated with convective transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state. It characterizes energy transport rather than the transport of particles alone. $$ v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)} = \frac{q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}}{w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}} $$ where $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the effective energy-convection velocity, $q_{E,\mathrm{conv}}^{(s)}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux associated with charge state $s$, and $w_{\mathrm{th}}^{(s)}$ is the corresponding thermal-energy density. The ratio is an energy-transport weighting and need not equal the [ion charge-state particle convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity). It is the thermal effective specialization of [ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection), including the more specific [effective thermal ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection).

rows.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
rows.description: Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, without restricting orbit class or spatial direction.
rows.documentation: Thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local vector source of angular momentum transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb collisions with other charged populations. It is the thermal-ion member of the broader [ion torque density due to collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) family. For the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional torque-density vector is defined from its distribution function by $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}) $$ where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion distribution function, and $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision operator. At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed orbit and spatial-direction contributions; [co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) are corresponding restrictions. It excludes torque deposited in fast-ion populations. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque-density component points along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
rows.description: Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over charge states and evaluated at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of all argon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral argon is excluded, and the value is not a volume average over the barrier or surrounding plasma. For argon charge states indexed by $q$, the velocity is defined by $$ v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow component along the toroidal unit vector. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing toroidally. The charge-state aggregation is the same as for [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier). Sign convention: Positive when the argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
rows.description: Signed toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered to bulk thermal electrons by collisions with co-passing particles.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the local collisional angular-momentum transfer delivered to the bulk thermal electron population by co-passing particles. It retains only the transfer along the geometric toroidal direction. The toroidal projection is defined by $$ \tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $\tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the full collisional torque-density vector transferred to thermal electrons from co-passing particles. The unprojected quantity is [co-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Non-toroidal components and transfers involving the counter-passing orbit class are excluded; the latter are represented by [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Sign convention: Positive when collisional angular-momentum transfer to thermal electrons points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
rows.description: Signed toroidal collisional torque per unit volume delivered to a specified bulk thermal-ion species by co-passing fast particles.
rows.documentation: Toroidal co-passing thermal-ion collisional torque density is the local toroidal component of the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to a specified bulk thermal-ion species through Coulomb collisions with co-passing fast particles. Its relation to the vector parent is $$ \tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the signed toroidal torque-density component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the [co-passing thermal-ion torque-density vector due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{co}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify the receiving ion species, co-passing contribution, and collisional mechanism, respectively. The co-passing restriction applies to the colliding fast-particle distribution, not to the orbit class of the receiving thermal ions. Counter-passing and trapped contributions are excluded. The quantity is local, without spatial averaging or volume integration. Ionic charge-state contributions are summed within the selected species, while different receiving ion species remain distinct; [co-passing thermal-ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) retains charge-state resolution in the corresponding vector quantity. This is a population- and component-resolved contribution to [torque density](name:torque_density). The adjacent [toroidal co-passing thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describes transfer to thermal electrons instead and is not included here. Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density component delivered to thermal ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density
rows.description: Local toroidal angular-momentum source density contributed by passing particles whose parallel motion follows the co-current direction.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the local toroidal component of torque density contributed by the co-passing particle population. It gives the source rate of toroidal angular momentum per unit volume for that orbit class. The toroidal torque density is defined by $$ \tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} $$ where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing toroidal torque density, $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the toroidal force-density component on co-passing particles. The parent [co-passing torque density](name:co_passing_torque_density) includes the corresponding angular-momentum source without selecting this toroidal component. This is a local quantity, not a flux-surface average, and is distinct from the [toroidal counter-passing torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density), which resolves the opposite passing-orbit branch. Sign convention: Positive when the co-passing force increases toroidal angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
rows.description: Volume-integrated toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque on fast ions in a selected charge state, equal to the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine symmetry axis from background plasma species.
rows.documentation: The toroidal scalar component of the volume-integrated torque vector exerted by Coulomb collisions on fast (suprathermal) ions in a single specified charge state. It represents the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine toroidal symmetry axis from background plasma species to this charge-state-resolved energetic ion population. $$ \tau_\phi = \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll}$ is the charge-state-resolved fast-ion collisional torque vector fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. This quantity covers only the suprathermal ion population in one charge state; the thermal-ion charge-state analog is [thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), the total charge-state collisional torque summed over all species is [total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), and the fast-ion toroidal torque summed over all charge states is [toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions). Sign convention: Positive when the collisional angular momentum transfer is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density
rows.description: Toroidal component of the net angular-momentum source density acting on a specified ion charge state.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque density acting on a specified ion species in a specified charge state. It represents the local source or sink of toroidal angular momentum, without attribution to a particular transport or collisional mechanism. $$ \tau_{\phi}^{i,q}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q} $$ where $\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}$ is the full torque-density vector for ion species $i$ and charge state $q$. The vector parent is [ion charge state torque density](name:ion_charge_state_torque_density). The quantity is a total over all contributing processes for the specified ion charge state; process-resolved contributions are distinct quantities. Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate
rows.description: Effective inverse relaxation time for dissipative decay of the toroidal bulk-flow momentum of a specified ion species, aggregated over its ionic charge states.
rows.documentation: The toroidal ion momentum damping rate quantifies dissipative relaxation of ordered toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species on magnetic flux surfaces. The toroidal direction follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. In a linear flow-damping closure, the damping contribution to the momentum balance is: $$ \left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{i,\phi}p_{i,\phi} $$ where $\nu_{i,\phi}$ is this damping rate, $p_{i,\phi}$ is the toroidal bulk-flow momentum density summed over the species' ionic charge states, $t$ is time, and the index $i$ identifies the ion species. The restricted derivative includes only the damping contribution. A constant positive rate produces exponential decay under this term alone. The coefficient applies to one ion species, not to the combined momentum of all plasma species. Its underlying bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, excluding neutral particles; the rate is an effective coefficient for that aggregate flow, not a sum of charge-state damping rates. The [toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) instead applies to a specified charge state. This quantity is the toroidal flow-component coefficient of the [ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). It describes relaxation rather than diffusive or convective transport of momentum between flux surfaces, and it excludes imposed momentum sources. The effective damping may include collisional, neoclassical, or anomalous contributions; no single mechanism is prescribed.

rows.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density
rows.description: Toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the torque density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. It is the state-resolved toroidal projection of neutral internal-state torque density, rather than a sum over all neutral internal states. $$ \tau_{\phi,s}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\left(\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_s\right) $$ where $\tau_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the machine symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_s$ is the force density exerted on the plasma by neutrals in internal state $s$. Summing this state-resolved quantity over all neutral internal states gives [toroidal neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density); it is distinct from the direction-independent [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density). Sign convention: Positive when the torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: torque_density
rows.description: Local vector rate of net angular-momentum transfer per unit volume to or from plasma, with population-, orbit-class-, mechanism-, and component-specific forms.
rows.documentation: Torque density is the local vector rate at which angular momentum is transferred to or from a specified plasma content, expressed per unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction unless a component-specific form is selected. The defining relation is $$ \boldsymbol{\tau} = \left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{transfer}} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ is the torque-density vector and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is the angular-momentum density of the selected plasma content. The transfer term is net over the mechanisms and populations included by the specific quantity. Population- and orbit-class-resolved instances include [ion torque density](name:ion_torque_density), [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density), and trapped or passing contributions; [toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) is the corresponding directional component. Sign convention: Positive when the torque vector points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis; the toroidal component is positive when it increases angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis
rows.description: Total ion number density at the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes, summed over all ion species and charge states.
rows.documentation: The total ion number density at the magnetic axis is the local number density of all ion species, including every ionic charge state. The magnetic axis is the innermost point of the nested closed flux surfaces, defined by a vanishing gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux. At the magnetic-axis position, the quantity is defined by $$ n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) $$ where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position, $s$ indexes ion species, and $Z$ indexes their ionic charge states. This is the all-ion aggregate of ion density at magnetic axis; it excludes electrons and neutral particles.

rows.name: total_ion_particle_source_rate
rows.description: Total ion particle source rate is the net ion addition or removal integrated over a plasma volume, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states.
rows.documentation: Total ion particle source rate is the net rate of ion production or loss, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states and integrated over a specified plasma volume. Its global value covers the entire plasma volume and supplies the source contribution to the total-ion particle-number balance. The integrated net rate is defined by $$ S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)=\int_V\sum_a\sum_{q\geq 1}\left(S_{a,q}^{+}-S_{a,q}^{-}\right)\,dV $$ where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}(V)$ is the total ion particle source rate in the integration region $V$, $a$ indexes ion species, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, $S_{a,q}^{+}$ and $S_{a,q}^{-}$ are the local volumetric ion production and removal rates for that species and charge state, and $dV$ is a physical volume element. The local rates combine all contributing source and sink processes. Each ion is counted once, without charge weighting; neutral particles are excluded from the ion count. Transitions between included ionic charge states cancel in the total, whereas conversion between neutral and ionized populations changes the ion count. Positive values indicate net ion addition and negative values indicate net removal. This is a particle-number source, not an electric-charge source or the full inventory change, which also includes transport across the integration boundary. This quantity is the species-summed, volume-integrated specialization of [ion particle source rate](name:ion_particle_source_rate). The [cumulative inside-flux-surface total ion particle source rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_total_ion_particle_source_rate) restricts the integration region to the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface; it recovers the global value when that region encompasses the entire plasma volume.

rows.name: total_trapped_particle_density
rows.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on magnetically trapped orbits, including both thermal and nonthermal particles.
rows.documentation: Total trapped-particle density is the flux-surface-averaged concentration of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These orbits undergo magnetic mirror reflection, reversing their motion parallel to the magnetic field rather than circulating as passing orbits. The flux-surface-averaged density is defined by $$ \langle n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}\rangle = \left\langle \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle $$ where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}$ is its local trapped-particle number density, and $f_s$ is its full thermal-plus-nonthermal velocity distribution. The vectors $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ denote position and particle velocity, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain corresponding to trapped orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. Angle brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic flux surface. The total includes both thermal and nonthermal trapped particles of the selected species; it does not sum over different species. Passing particles are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average, not a local density or a volume-integrated particle count. It equals the sum of the thermal trapped-particle contribution and the nonthermal contribution represented by [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), with both contributions averaged over the same magnetic flux surface.

rows.name: trapped_fast_particle_pressure
rows.description: Scalar trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by the total suprathermal population on magnetically trapped orbits. It combines field-aligned and transverse stress contributions and may be evaluated locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: Trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure); taking the scalar trace does not require the field-aligned and transverse stresses to be equal. At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local pressure is defined by the trapped-particle second velocity moment: $$ p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s \int_{\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}$ is the trapped fast-particle pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $c$ labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed, $f_{s,c}$ is the distribution function for suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain of those particles on magnetically trapped orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration element. The quantity applies to the total suprathermal population: contributions are added over fast-particle species and summed over all charge states, not density-weighted across charge states. It excludes thermal particles and fast particles on co-passing or counter-passing orbits. The local value retains spatial variation; flux-surface averaging gives an average over the surface and is not part of the trapped-orbit selection itself. The [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the field-aligned stress component, and the [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the mean stress per transverse degree of freedom for the same population. Their relation to the scalar trace is $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}})/3$. For a common population and spatial aggregation, the trapped contribution together with [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) sums to the [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) when those orbit classes partition the population.

rows.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
rows.description: Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume from trapped nonthermal particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state.
rows.documentation: Trapped thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate of kinetic-energy transfer from trapped fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state. Trapped guiding-center trajectories undergo magnetic-mirror reflection rather than continuous passing transit. The trapped restriction applies to the donating distribution, not to the orbits of the receiving thermal ions. The contribution is the flux-surface average of the receiving population's kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator: $$ P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\rho) = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_{i q}v^2 C_{i q,a}\!\left[f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}\right] \, d^3v \right\rangle_\rho $$ where $P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this collisional power density, $\rho$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $q$ is its specified ionic charge number, and $m_{i q}$ is the receiving ion mass. The vector $\mathbf{v}$ is the receiving ion velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration measure. The distribution $f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes the receiving thermal ions, while $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped part of the nonthermal donor distribution for species $a$. The operator $C_{i q,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution due to that donor species. Brackets denote the normalized flux-surface average, equivalently the limiting volume average over an infinitesimally thin shell surrounding the surface. The donor sum includes the nonthermal species represented in the collisional exchange; the receiving contribution is restricted to one species and charge state and is not summed over charge states. This is an energy-exchange source or sink, not stored kinetic-energy density or energy transfer through ionization or internal-state transitions. Adding the [co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) contributions to this trapped contribution recovers the flux-surface average of the [thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), which includes all donor orbit classes. Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the trapped nonthermal particles to the receiving thermal ions; negative when energy is transferred in the reverse direction.

rows.name: vertical_electron_velocity
rows.description: Signed height-axis component of the local electron-fluid bulk flow in the edge plasma, parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.
rows.documentation: The vertical electron velocity is the height-axis projection of the local bulk electron flow in the edge plasma. It represents directed electron motion after averaging over particle velocities, rather than random thermal motion. The defining projection is $$ u_{e,Z} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $u_{e,Z}$ is the vertical electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the local bulk [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The underlying bulk flow is the particle-density-weighted mean electron velocity at each position; no spatial averaging is implied. This signed component is distinct from the electron speed, thermal velocity spread, and particle flux. The vertical direction is geometric and need not coincide with the local magnetic-field direction. Together with [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) and [toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it specifies the cylindrical components of the electron-flow vector. Sign convention: Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

rows.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity
rows.description: Mean edge-plasma ion flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, resolved for one specified species and ionization charge state.
rows.documentation: The vertical ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the local bulk flow of a specified ion species and ionization charge state onto the vertical direction. It describes directed motion in the edge plasma in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the vertical component of the [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), defined by the first velocity moment: $$ u_{s,q,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{s,q}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{s,q}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{s,q,Z}$ is the vertical bulk-flow component, $\mathbf u_{s,q}$ is the bulk velocity vector, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its ionization charge number, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,q}$ is the selected population's phase-space number density. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. Both integrals cover particle velocity space; the definition requires nonzero population density. Only the selected ion species and charge-state population contribute; neutral particles and other species are excluded. If a charge-state bundle is specified, its distribution combines the member states, giving their number-density-weighted mean velocity rather than a sum of velocities. This quantity is a signed flow component, not a speed, thermal velocity spread, or particle flux; the vertical direction is not generally the poloidal or magnetic-field-parallel direction. The [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity) is instead the density-weighted mean of these components over all ionic charge states of the species. Sign convention: Positive when the selected ion population's bulk flow has a component toward increasing $Z$.

rows.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
rows.description: Signed vertical projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from individual guiding-center motion.
rows.documentation: The vertical ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of individual ions. For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial pressure, the defining projection is: $$ v_{\ast\alpha,Z} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $v_{\ast\alpha,Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic-drift velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the toroidal symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, its geometric vertical component, like its [toroidal component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), need not vanish. The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of that species. Its vertical projection is therefore the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state vertical components, not their sum. Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified ion charge state has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

rows.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
rows.description: Vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport rate of vertical linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state. It is the vertical-vertical component of the neutral momentum-flux tensor for that state.
rows.documentation: The vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is the $ZZ$ component of the state-resolved momentum-flux tensor, not a particle flux or a local momentum source. For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the vertical component is defined by $$ \Pi_{ZZ}^{(s)} = \hat{Z} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{Z} = \int m_s v_Z^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $m_s$ is the mass of a neutral particle in state $s$, $v_Z=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{Z}$ is the vertical velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution. The vertical direction is the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not the radial, toroidal, or magnetic-field-parallel direction. As a diagonal $ZZ$ tensor component formed from $v_Z^2$, this quantity is nonnegative for any nonnegative state-resolved velocity distribution. This component is the vertical member of the parent neutral internal-state momentum flux, differs from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [parallel](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and linear internal-state components, and is the state-resolved counterpart of [vertical neutral momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux).

rows.name: vertical_neutral_velocity
rows.description: Mean directed motion of a selected neutral species along the vertical symmetry-axis direction, averaged over contributing internal states with number-density weighting.
rows.documentation: The vertical neutral velocity is the projection of the bulk drift of a selected neutral species onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents directed motion after averaging over particle velocities and contributing internal states. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position, its local definition is: $$ u_{0,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\mathbf v\,f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{0,Z}$ is the vertical neutral velocity, $\mathbf u_0$ is the [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector, $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of neutral internal state $a$, and $\mathcal A$ is the set of contributing internal states. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The state distributions combine with number-density weighting for one selected neutral species, not by summing state velocities or averaging different species together. This is a local flow component, including for neutrals in the scrape-off layer and divertor, rather than a spatial average, flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, or random thermal spread. Unlike [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which retains one specified internal state, this quantity averages over the contributing internal states before taking the vertical projection. Sign convention: Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward increasing vertical position $Z$.

rows.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
rows.description: Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture, formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
rows.documentation: Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume. The defining relation is $$ Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge, $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position, with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct from an ordinary ion charge average. This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma boundary, which averages the local effective charge over a boundary surface, and from [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which represents an ordinary ion charge number rather than the second charge moment normalized by free-electron density.

rows.name: volume_averaged_helium_4_density
rows.description: Volume-averaged number density of helium-4 ions over the confined plasma volume, providing a global measure of fusion-ash concentration in deuterium-tritium plasmas.
rows.documentation: The volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of fusion-ash ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the global counterpart of the local [helium-4 ion density](name:helium_4_density) and is distinct from the chord mean [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density). The volume average is defined by $$ \overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r} $$ where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local helium-4 ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. The helium-4 ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while neutral helium is excluded. Its ratio to the volume-averaged electron density is defined by [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

rows.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge
rows.description: Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population.
rows.documentation: Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population. It is a normalized volume average representing the global mean ionization level of that selected charge state. For ion species $i$, the volume-averaged ion charge is defined by $$ \langle Z_{\mathrm{dom},i} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\Omega}\int_\Omega Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [ion charge](name:ion_charge) number of the dominant ionization state of species $i$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega$ is the confined plasma volume, and $V_\Omega$ is the volume of $\Omega$. The population is one specified ion species; if the species represents a lumped-ion population, the same definition applies to that lumped population. The charge-state convention is dominant-state selection: the quantity is not a charge-state sum and is not the density-weighted mean over all charge states. This quantity differs from [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number), which represents the density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states of the ion species. It also differs from [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), which is a particle population density rather than a charge number.

rows.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
rows.description: Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
rows.documentation: Number density of ion The volume average of the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is defined by $$ \langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV $$ where $i$ labels the specified ion species, $n_i$ is its local ion number density, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element. The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and includes thermal and nonthermal ions; neutral particles are excluded. This is a single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean. Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of ions of the specified species within that volume. The [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is a species-specific instance of the same averaging definition.

rows.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature
rows.description: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all included species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
rows.documentation: The volume-averaged total ion temperature is the volume average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy. The volume average is defined by $$ \overline{T}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\int_V T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV}{\int_V dV} $$ where $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is its differential volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local quantity defined by [total_ion_temperature](name:total_ion_temperature). Species and charge-state density weighting is performed locally before the volume averaging. Unlike [line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity averages over volume rather than along a plasma chord.

rows.name: volume_integrated_particle_source_rate
rows.description: Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net number of particles added to a specified distribution per unit time by a source contribution over the plasma volume.
rows.documentation: Volume-integrated particle source rate is the net particle-number input to a specified particle distribution from a given source contribution, integrated over the plasma volume. The defining volume integral is $$ S(t) = \int_V s_p(\mathbf{x},t)\,d^3x $$ where $S$ is the volume-integrated particle source rate, $t$ is time, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $d^3x$ is the volume element, and $s_p$ is the local net particle source rate per physical volume. For a kinetic source term, $s_p$ is its velocity-space integral, the particle-number moment. The rate applies to the species and population represented by the specified distribution. Volume integration does not imply summation over other distributions, species, or source mechanisms. For a distribution-function-driven contribution, it is the volume integral of the [particle source rate due to distribution-function-driven processes](name:particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven), not its volume average. No restriction to thermal particles or thermalization is implied. When the contribution describes thermalization, it counts transfer from fast particles into the thermal background, rather than particle creation in the combined populations; reverse transfer constitutes a sink for the thermal population. Sign convention: Positive when the source contribution adds particles to the specified distribution; negative when it removes particles.

rows.name: electron_density_at_outboard_midplane
rows.description: Electron particle number density at the low-field-side intersection of a magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
rows.documentation: Electron number density at the outboard midplane is the local density of the electron population at the low-field-side intersection of a specified magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane. It is the electron-specific member of density_at_outboard_midplane. At that location, the density is defined by the zeroth velocity-space moment $$ n_e(R,\phi,Z)=\int f_e(R,\phi,Z,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_e$ is electron number density, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The position is described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity counts electrons only and is distinct from total particle density and from electron density evaluated at the magnetic axis.

rows.name: momentum_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
rows.description: Momentum flux due to E cross B drift is the dimensionless scalar transport of a selected component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface by the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It fixes the drift mechanism and dimensionless status while abstracting over the momentum component, surface-normal direction, averaging, and choice of normalization reference supplied by concrete specializations.
rows.documentation: Momentum flux due to $E\times B$ drift is the scalar transport of a selected component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface carried by the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed in dimensionless form relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It represents the $E\times B$ advective transport channel of momentum, not an unspecified or total momentum-transport channel. The dimensionless scalar component is the surface-normal advective flux of the selected momentum density divided by a reference momentum-flux scale: $$ \Pi_{\alpha}^{E\times B} = \frac{\left\langle p_{\alpha}\, \mathbf{v}_{E\times B}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} \right\rangle}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}} $$ where $p_{\alpha}$ is the selected component of linear plasma momentum density, $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$ is the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen oriented surface normal, $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the aggregation or averaging convention specified by the concrete quantity, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum-flux scale relative to which the quantity is expressed. This quantity fixes two things: the driving mechanism is the $E\times B$ drift, and the quantity is dimensionless, being expressed relative to a reference scale. It abstracts over the remaining axes: the transported momentum component $\alpha$, the orientation of the crossing surface, the population or velocity-space contribution included in $p_{\alpha}$, the averaging convention, and the specific choice of $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Concrete specializations fix these axes. This is a flux of momentum, not the momentum density itself, not a force or torque density, and not the full momentum-flux tensor. It excludes momentum transport carried by parallel streaming, magnetic drifts, diamagnetic flows, collisional viscosity, or external forces except where those effects are part of the selected momentum density or of the fields that determine the $E\times B$ drift. The [normalized momentum flux due to $E\times B$ drift](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the specialization that explicitly designates a reference normalization as part of its identity; the present quantity is the mechanism-level abstraction under which any such normalized member sits, without itself selecting which reference scale, momentum component, surface, or averaging is used. Sign convention: Positive when positive selected linear momentum is advected by the $E\times B$ drift through the oriented surface in the direction of the chosen positive surface normal, or equivalently when negative selected linear momentum is advected opposite to that normal.

rows.name: normalized_collisionality
rows.description: Dimensionless ratio of a specified interspecies collision frequency to the characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce frequency used for the plasma population.
rows.documentation:
This collisionality measures the strength of interspecies collisional relaxation relative to collisionless motion along magnetic-field trajectories. $$ 
u_{ab}^{*} =  rac{
u_{ab}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}} $$ where $
u_{ab}$ is the collision frequency between species $a$ and $b$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the relevant characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce angular frequency; both quantities have reciprocal-time units. The denominator must be interpreted according to the selected orbit or motion class, so this quantity is distinct from the collision frequency itself. It generalizes the population-specific electron collisionality and complements collisionality at the pedestal top when the characteristic frequency is evaluated there.

rows.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density
rows.description: Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter-density fluctuation response, distinct from a gyroaveraged particle-density perturbation.
rows.documentation: Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter density fluctuation response; the normalization removes the scale of the reference density while preserving perturbation amplitude and phase. For magnetic moment $\mu = m_s v_\perp^2/(2B)$, the normalized moment is defined by: $$ \widehat{n}_{gc,s} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{0}^{\infty} \delta f_{gc,s}(v_\parallel,\mu)\,\frac{2\pi B}{m_s}\,d\mu\,dv_\parallel $$ where $\widehat{n}_{gc,s}$ is the normalized gyrocenter perturbed density for species $s$, $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the positive reference number density for that species, $\delta f_{gc,s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution with respect to ordinary velocity-space volume, $B$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude, $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $v_\perp$ is speed perpendicular to the magnetic field, and $\mu$ is magnetic moment. The factor $2\pi B/m_s$ is the gyroangle-integrated velocity-space Jacobian for this definition of $\mu$. For a species represented by multiple charge states, the perturbed gyrocenter-density numerator and the reference density are charge-state-summed before the ratio is formed. This quantity excludes any Bessel-function or finite-Larmor-radius weighting inside the velocity-space integral; that weighted moment is the normalized gyrocenter gyroaveraged density. The dimensional numerator of the ratio is the unnormalized gyrocenter-density perturbation; the related perturbed gyrocenter density denotes a dimensionless gyrocenter-density perturbation in the same family. The normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the corresponding perturbed pressure moment. For complex perturbation amplitudes, the integral is taken over the complex amplitude; the arbitrary overall mode phase is external to the definition. Sign convention: Positive when, for a real perturbation amplitude, the velocity-space integral of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution gives an excess gyrocenter density relative to the positive reference density.

rows.name: normalized_particle_charge
rows.description: Dimensionless charge number of a particle species, obtained by dividing its physical charge by the positive reference charge used for normalization.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the normalized form of particle charge for a particle species. It preserves the sign of the physical charge and expresses its magnitude relative to a common positive reference charge. The normalized charge is defined by $$ q_{\rm n} = \frac{q}{q_{\rm ref}} $$ where $q$ is the species' physical electric charge and $q_{\rm ref}$ is the strictly positive reference charge, both expressed in the same charge units. The result is dimensionless and is used as the charge-coupling coefficient in normalized electromagnetic and electrostatic equations. Its sign distinguishes positive and negative charge, while its magnitude gives the charge relative to the selected reference.

rows.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
rows.description: Dimensionless vector of normalized energy-weighted velocity-space moments of a species' perturbed particle distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the normalized particle energy moment of a species' perturbed velocity distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its components use distinct squared velocity-direction weights while sharing an energy-weighted normalization from the corresponding unperturbed species distribution. For species $s$ and selected velocity direction or weighting component $a$, the normalized moment is defined by $$ \mathcal{E}_{a,s} = \frac{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v_a^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v^4 f_{0s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v} $$ where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v$ is its magnitude, $v_a$ is the selected velocity component, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution, $f_{0s}$ is the unperturbed distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The quantity is a particle moment, distinct from gyrocenter moments and from unweighted density or pressure moments. The [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) is its perpendicular directional realization.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_current_density_bessel_1
rows.description: Dimensionless first-Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution, capturing its field-aligned finite-Larmor-radius response.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the first-order Bessel-weighted, field-parallel current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution. It represents the electromagnetic response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the gyrocenter description. The normalized moment is defined by $$ j_{parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q}{j_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int v_{\parallel} J_1(k_{\perp}\rho)\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $j_{\parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment, $q$ is the charge of the represented particle species, $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference current-density scale, $v_{\parallel}$ is the velocity component along the local equilibrium magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function of the first kind, $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho$ is the particle gyroradius, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space coordinate, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The quantity is restricted to the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, the field-parallel velocity channel, and the first-order Bessel weighting. Its aggregation convention is the charge-weighted moment shown in the integral; it is not an unweighted density moment, a perpendicular current channel, an equilibrium contribution, or a particle-frame moment. It is the normalized, parallel specialization of the vector [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density), with the additional $J_1$ finite-Larmor-radius weighting. Removing that weighting gives the corresponding [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density). Sign convention: Positive when the charge-weighted perturbed current is directed along the local equilibrium magnetic field, whose orientation is expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
rows.description: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the dimensionless velocity-space moment of a species' perturbed distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the perpendicular speed squared times the total speed squared and normalized to the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment of the same species.
rows.documentation: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the perpendicular member of the particle perturbed-energy moment family for a species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its velocity-space weight is the perpendicular speed squared multiplied by the total speed squared, and the reference normalization is the corresponding unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment. The quantity is defined as the ratio of the weighted perturbed moment to the unperturbed reference moment: $$ M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, v^2\, f_{0,s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v} $$ where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, $v_\parallel$ is the particle speed parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, $v^2 = v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total particle speed squared, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution of the eigenmode, $f_{0,s}$ is the unperturbed (equilibrium) particle distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The denominator is the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment shared by the parent [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) and its parallel counterpart, so the parallel and perpendicular members are directly comparable. This scalar is the perpendicular entry of the [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) decomposition and is paired with the parallel normalized particle perturbed energy evaluated with the same perturbed distribution and normalization. It is distinct from the [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), whose weight is the perpendicular speed squared alone: the energy moment retains the additional total-speed-squared factor. Because a linear eigenmode carries an arbitrary complex amplitude, only comparisons made under the same eigenmode amplitude and phase convention are physically meaningful. Sign convention: Positive when the velocity-space integral of $\tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s$ is positive under the chosen eigenmode phase convention.

rows.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
rows.description: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function J1.
rows.documentation: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function. It is the perpendicular projection of the Bessel-1 normalized perturbed pressure moment, associated with particle kinetic energy perpendicular to the background magnetic field. The normalized moment is defined by $$ \hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2}\, J_1\!\left(k_\perp \rho(v_\perp)\right)\, \delta f_\mathrm{gc}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v $$ where $\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1}$ is the normalized perpendicular Bessel-1 pressure perturbation, $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference thermal pressure, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference density, $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference temperature expressed as particle energy, $m$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the background magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function, $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho(v_\perp)$ is the velocity-dependent gyroradius, $\delta f_\mathrm{gc}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is the perpendicular pressure-tensor projection of [normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1); the complementary field-aligned projection is parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1. It differs from perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure by the first-order Bessel weighting and from perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure by representing the Bessel-1 finite-Larmor-radius contribution rather than the unweighted gyrocenter moment. Sign convention: Positive when, after the eigenmode phase has been fixed by the chosen reference perturbation, the real part of the defining Bessel-weighted perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment represents an excess over the equilibrium gyrocenter distribution.

rows.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature
rows.description: Dimensionless ratio comparing a particle species’ kinetic temperature with the positive reference temperature on the same magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: The quantity expresses the kinetic temperature of a selected particle species relative to a single reference thermal scale on the same magnetic flux surface. It is the normalized counterpart of [particle temperature](name:particle_temperature), while retaining the species dependence of the numerator. It is defined by $$ T_p^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{T_p}{T_{\mathrm{ref}}} $$ where $T_p$ is the kinetic temperature of the selected particle species and $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference temperature for the flux surface. The ratio is dimensionless and is not an absolute temperature; its value depends on the specified reference temperature.

rows.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field
rows.description: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at the reference point whose major radius is the reference major radius, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at a specified reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The reference point has major radius equal to the [reference major radius](name:reference_major_radius). The defining projection is: $$ B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) $$ where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the toroidal reference magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}=(R_{\mathrm{ref}},\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},Z_{\mathrm{ref}})$ is the full reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$. For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the value is independent of $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$. This quantity is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field). It is distinct from [toroidal magnetic field at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis), from the magnetic-field magnitude, and from [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field). Sign convention: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
rows.description: Complex phasor of the E-plus left-hand circular polarization component of an electromagnetic-wave electric field in a magnetized plasma.
rows.documentation: The left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field is the E-plus complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the circular polarization basis transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It retains both polarization amplitude and phase and is a component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field). Using the negative-time-harmonic convention, the component is defined by $$ E_{+}=\mathbf{E}_{w}\cdot\mathbf{e}_{+}^{*},\qquad \mathbf{e}_{+}=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}+i\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}}{\sqrt{2}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}=\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_{0}}{|\mathbf{B}_{0}|} $$ where $\mathbf{E}_{w}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{B}_{0}$ is the local background magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction, the transverse unit vectors $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}$ form a right-handed basis, and the asterisk denotes complex conjugation. The associated physical field uses $\exp(-i\omega t)$, so this component carries phase information rather than representing a field magnitude. Its real-part sibling [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field real part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part) provides one quadrature, while the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) represents the opposite circular polarization.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
rows.description: Power-deposition-weighted flux-surface amplitude of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus wave-electric-field phasor for each toroidal mode number.
rows.documentation: This quantity is the nonnegative amplitude of the right-hand circularly polarized (E-minus, or R-wave) component of a coherent wave electric-field phasor. It represents the mode-resolved field strength after power-deposition-weighted averaging over a magnetic flux surface. For toroidal mode number $n$, the amplitude is defined by $$ \mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}} = \left|\frac{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\,\widetilde{E}_{-,n}\rangle_{\psi}}{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle_{\psi}}\right| $$ where $\mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude of the E-minus wave-electric-field component, $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $\widetilde{E}_{-,n}$ is its complex phasor, $p_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the power-deposition density, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average, and $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface. The definition applies where the power-deposition-weighted denominator is nonzero. The quantity is restricted to the right-hand circular polarization and to one toroidal mode at a time. It excludes the left-hand circularly polarized component, the total electric-field amplitude obtained by combining polarizations, and an unweighted average or an average of pointwise amplitudes; the modulus is taken after the weighted complex averaging. It is the toroidal-mode-resolved amplitude specialization of the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field amplitude](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude). The corresponding complex E-minus phasor is described by the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), while this quantity retains only its amplitude.

rows.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
rows.description: Amplitude representation of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus component of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor, retaining its polarization direction while removing its complex phase.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the amplitude-form representation of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus contribution to a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric field. It retains the polarization basis direction and field strength while excluding the phasor phase. $$ \mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}} = |\tilde{E}_{-}|\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-} $$ Here, $\mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude representation of the polarized field component, $\tilde{E}_{-}$ is the complex E-minus coefficient of the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-}$ is the right-hand circular polarization unit vector transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field. The quantity applies specifically to the right-hand E-minus polarization and excludes the left-hand E-plus component, represented by the [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field). It is an amplitude rather than the full complex phasor and therefore does not retain phase information; it is also distinct from the separate real and imaginary quadratures. The parent quantity imposes no toroidal-mode resolution, flux-surface aggregation, or power-deposition weighting. The [per-toroidal-mode right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field amplitude](name:per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude) is a specialization that applies those operations to this common amplitude quantity.

rows.name: total_absorbed_wave_power
rows.description: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to all plasma particle populations and integrated over all spatial locations.
