rows.documentation: Total absorbed wave power is the total rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to all plasma particle populations, with contributions integrated over the plasma volume. $$ P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves} $$ where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the combined energy of all included plasma particle populations, $t$ is time, and the subscript “waves” restricts the derivative to direct energy transfer from the coherent electromagnetic-wave field. This quantity is globally aggregated: it is summed over all species, charge states, populations, and spatial locations. It includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes electromagnetic power that remains in the wave field and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by collisions. It is the species-summed specialization of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), unlike [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), which is restricted to electron populations. It is also the global counterpart of [total absorbed wave power at the inside flux surface](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which retains only the power enclosed within a selected flux surface; Fourier-resolved contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode total absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power).

rows.name: total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface
rows.description: Cumulative power transferred from electromagnetic waves to electrons, ions, and fast populations within a selected magnetic flux surface.
rows.documentation: Cumulative absorbed electromagnetic-wave power deposited in the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface. It includes absorption by electron, ion, and fast populations and represents an enclosed quantity rather than a local power density. The defining relation is $$ P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power, $\psi$ is the label of the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that surface, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total absorbed wave power density at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$ summed over electrons, ions, and fast populations, and $dV$ is the differential volume element. This quantity is cumulative over the enclosed volume and is not a local deposition density or a population-resolved contribution. Population-specific quantities such as [thermal electron power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [thermal ion power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) resolve components of this aggregate. When the selected surface encloses the full absorbing plasma volume, it equals [total absorbed wave power](name:total_absorbed_wave_power).

rows.name: vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_beam
rows.description: Vertical Z coordinate of a beam-tracing beam position along its propagation path, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
rows.documentation: The quantity is the vertical coordinate of a ray or beam position evaluated along the propagation path of a beam-tracing beam. It identifies the position's height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coordinate is the projection of the beam position onto the vertical direction: $$ z = \mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{Z} $$ where $z$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of the beam point, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical frame. This quantity applies to each beam position along the propagation path and is not aggregated over path positions or over multiple rays or beams. It describes geometric location only; it is not a wave amplitude, magnetic or electric field component, or propagation-direction quantity. It is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the launching position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position), which identifies the beam's physical launch point rather than a general position along the path. At the launch point, the two coordinates may have the same value.
